add_board_outline.name: add_board_outline
add_board_outline.description: Draw the PCB board outline (Edge.Cuts layer) as a rectangle, rounded rectangle, circle or polygon.

x.description: X coordinate of top-left corner for rectangles (default: 0)

y.description: Y coordinate of top-left corner for rectangles (default: 0)

add_board_text.name: add_board_text
add_board_text.description: Add a text label to a PCB layer (e.g. silkscreen, fab, courtyard). Also the way to annotate or comment a component: place the text next to it, e.g. on F.Fab.

position.description: Position of the text

layer.description: Layer to place the text on

add_component_3d_model.name: add_component_3d_model
add_component_3d_model.description: Attach a 3D model to one or more PLACED footprints on the open board, live via the KiCAD IPC API (changes appear instantly, no file conflicts). Use this for components already on the PCB; for a library .kicad_mod use add_footprint_3d_model.

reference.description: Footprint reference(s), e.g. 'D1', ['D1','D2'], or '*' for all footprints

replace.description: Replace an existing model with the same filename (default true)

add_copper.name: add_copper
add_copper.description: Add tracks (polylines) and vias in one all-or-nothing batch (MCP_ISSUES E1). Items: {track: {net, layer, width, points: [[x,y],...]}}, {via: {net, at: [x,y], size, drill, layers?: [top, bottom]}}, or spec strings 'T net layer width x1 y1 x2 y2 ...' / 'V net x y [size drill]' (mm; layer F/B/In1 shorthands ok; width/size/drill default to the board's current values). Every item is validated first; any error adds nothing. Returns {success, message, added: {trackSegments, vias}, items, uuids, drc?}.

locked.description: Lock the new copper (default false); lock hand routing before autorouting

dryRun.description: Validate and report the would-be change without touching the board

drcDelta.description: Save now and run DRC (project rules) to report violations this edit added/resolved (slower: one DRC, two when the last recorded run is stale)

refillZones.description: Refill zones in the drcDelta DRC run (default true)

projectPath.description: .kicad_pro whose rules the drcDelta DRC uses (default: the board's project)

add_copper_pour.name: add_copper_pour
add_copper_pour.description: Add a copper pour (ground/power plane) to the PCB. Coordinates and sizes are mm. For several layers or a named zone use add_zone. Returns {success, message, pour: {layer, net, clearance, minWidth, priority, fillType, pointCount, padConnection?, ...}}.

layer.description: PCB layer

outline.description: Array of {x, y} points in mm defining the pour boundary. If omitted, the board outline is used.

padConnection.description: How pads connect to the pour

thermalSpokeWidth.description: Thermal relief spoke width in mm

add_drc_rule.name: add_drc_rule
add_drc_rule.description: Append KiCad custom DRC rule(s) to the project's .kicad_dru with feedback (MCP_ISSUES C2). Checks syntax (including value forms KiCad 10 silently rejects: unitless lengths, '(min 2)' for min_resolved_spokes), then runs kicad-cli DRC on temporary copies before and after the change with a canary rule, so a rules file KiCad drops is caught and nothing is written. Reports how many items the rule's condition matches (assertion probe; capped at 199), violations citing it, and new/resolved violations. Returns {success, message, kicadAccepted, matched, drc: {before, after, citingRule, newCount, resolvedCount, new, resolved}, written, notes, warnings}.

ruleText.description: One or more rules, e.g. (rule "x" (condition "A.NetName == 'GND'") (constraint clearance (min 0.2mm)))

replace.description: Replace existing rules with the same names

dryRun.description: Check and measure, but don't write

measure.description: Run the kicad-cli checks (default true; false = syntax check only)

refillZones.description: Refill zones in the measuring DRC (default true)

limit.description: Max new/resolved items listed (default 10)

projectPath.description: .kicad_pro whose .kicad_dru to edit

add_footprint_3d_model.name: add_footprint_3d_model
add_footprint_3d_model.description: Attach (or replace) a 3D model — .step/.stp/.wrl — to a .kicad_mod footprint file. KiCAD path variables like ${KIPRJMOD} or ${KICAD10_3DMODEL_DIR} are supported. Use this after create_footprint so the part shows up in the 3D viewer (Alt+3).

footprintPath.description: Full path to the .kicad_mod file, e.g. C:/MyLib.pretty/MyPart.kicad_mod

modelPath.description: Path to the 3D model file. Prefer ${KIPRJMOD}/MyProj.3dshapes/MyPart.step for portability.

replace.description: Replace an existing model with the same filename (default true)

add_gnd_stitching_vias.name: add_gnd_stitching_vias
add_gnd_stitching_vias.description: Drop GND stitching vias across the board with collision checking against every non-GND segment, via, and pad on every copper layer (PTH vias penetrate the full stackup, so missing any one layer is the classic silent-short failure mode). Three combinable strategies: `grid` (regular grid across the interior), `around_refs` (densify around named ICs), and `in_zones` (only place vias inside an actual GND copper zone). Supports `dryRun` to preview placements without writing.

gndNet.description: Name of the ground net (default: auto-detect GND / GROUND / VSS / /GND).

strategies.description: Which placement strategies to combine (default: ['grid']). Pass ['grid', 'around_refs', 'in_zones'] for full coverage.

viaDrill.description: Via drill diameter in mm (default 0.3). Must be smaller than viaSize.

clearance.description: Extra clearance beyond required between each new via and existing copper, in mm (default 0.2).

spacing.description: Grid spacing in mm for `grid` and `around_refs` strategies (default 5.0).

densifyRefs.description: Reference designators to densify ground around (used by `around_refs`). Targets: MCUs, switching regulators, RF parts.

densifyRadius.description: How many grid cells around each ref to try (default 2 = 5x5 candidate field per ref).

edgeMargin.description: Keep-out from the board edge in mm (default 0.5).

maxVias.description: Cap on total placements across all strategies (default unlimited).

dryRun.description: If true, return the placements that would be made but don't modify the board (default false).

add_hierarchical_sheet.name: add_hierarchical_sheet
add_hierarchical_sheet.description: Insert a hierarchical-sheet reference block into a parent schematic, pointing at an existing sub-sheet file. Adds the sheet box, name/file fields, a sheet_instances path entry on the next page number, and fixes sub-sheet component instance paths so ERC resolves references.

subsheetPath.description: Path to the existing sub-sheet .kicad_sch to reference

position.description: Top-left of the sheet box in mm (default 50,50)

add_layer.name: add_layer
add_layer.description: Add a new copper or technical layer to the PCB stackup.

position.description: Layer position

add_library_symbol_property.name: add_library_symbol_property
add_library_symbol_property.description: Add or update a custom property (Manufacturer, MPN, LCSC, etc.) on a symbol definition in the lib_symbols section. This makes the property available to all instances of that symbol in the schematic.

position.description: Position {x, y} in mm (default: 0, 0)

add_mounting_hole.name: add_mounting_hole
add_mounting_hole.description: Place a mounting hole (NPTH or PTH) at the specified position on the PCB.

position.description: Position of the mounting hole

padDiameter.description: Optional diameter of the pad around the hole

add_net.name: add_net
add_net.description: Create a new net on the PCB

add_no_connect.name: add_no_connect
add_no_connect.description: Add a no-connect flag (X marker) to a pin that is intentionally left unconnected. This suppresses ERC 'Pin not connected' errors for unused pins. PREFERRED: supply componentRef + pinNumber to snap to the exact pin endpoint. Alternatively supply position [x, y] in mm matching the pin endpoint exactly.

position.description: Position [x, y] in mm. Required when componentRef/pinNumber are not given.

componentRef.description: Component reference to snap to (e.g. U1, R1). Use with pinNumber.

pinNumber.description: Pin number or name on componentRef (e.g. '1', 'GND'). Use with componentRef.

add_pin_labels.name: add_pin_labels
add_pin_labels.description: Add silkscreen text labels next to chosen pads of one footprint (e.g. connector pin names). For each pad it tries the requested side (auto = away from the part body, outside its courtyard), horizontal text first at growing offsets, then rotated, then the other sides, and keeps the first spot that clears pads, silk, courtyards and the board edge (stroke geometry). Labels go on the footprint's silk side as board text. Units mm. Returns {ref, layer, placed:[{pad,text,x,y,angle,side}], skipped:[{pad,text,reason}], saved}.

side.description: Preferred side of each pad (default auto)

textThickness.description: Stroke thickness in mm (default 0.15 x height)

gap.description: Clearance to pads and other silk, mm (default 0.15)

offset.description: Distance from the pad edge to the label, mm (default 0.3)

edgeClearance.description: Clearance to the board edge, mm (default 0.25)

avoidBody.description: Keep labels out of courtyards, the connector's own included (default true)

layer.description: Silk layer override, F.SilkS or B.SilkS (default: the footprint's side)

dryRun.description: Report the label positions without changing the board

add_rule_area.name: add_rule_area
add_rule_area.description: Add a rule area (keepout) on copper layers forbidding tracks, vias, pads, pours and/or footprints (MCP_ISSUES E3). Layers accept 'F.Cu', 'In1', or '*.Cu' for all. Returns {success, message, ruleArea: {uuid, name, layers, forbid, areaMm2}, drc?}.

polygon.description: Polygon [[x, y], ...] (mm), a box {x1, y1, x2, y2}, or "board" for the board outline

name.description: Rule area name (usable in DRC rules and edit_zone)

dryRun.description: Validate and report the would-be change without touching the board

drcDelta.description: Save now and run DRC (project rules) to report violations this edit added/resolved (slower: one DRC, two when the last recorded run is stale)

refillZones.description: Refill zones in the drcDelta DRC run (default true)

projectPath.description: .kicad_pro whose rules the drcDelta DRC uses (default: the board's project)

add_schematic_component.name: add_schematic_component
add_schematic_component.description: Add a component to the schematic. Symbol format is 'Library:SymbolName' (e.g., 'Device:R', 'EDA-MCP:ESP32-C3')

position.description: Position on schematic

unit.description: Unit number for multi-unit symbols (1=A, 2=B, 3=C, …). Defaults to 1.

angle.description: Rotation angle in degrees (KiCad CCW). 0=vertical resistor, 90=horizontal. Defaults to 0.

mirrorY.description: Mirror the symbol horizontally (flip left-right). Useful for transistors facing opposite direction.

add_schematic_hierarchical_label.name: add_schematic_hierarchical_label
add_schematic_hierarchical_label.description: Add a hierarchical label (sheet interface port) to a sub-sheet schematic. Hierarchical labels are the connection points that link a sub-sheet to its parent via sheet pins. The label text must exactly match the corresponding sheet pin name.

text.description: Label text (e.g. 'SD_CLK') — must match the sheet pin name

position.description: Position [x, y] in mm

shape.description: Signal direction from the sub-sheet's perspective

orientation.description: Rotation in degrees: 0=label points right, 180=label points left (default: 0)

add_schematic_net_label.name: add_schematic_net_label
add_schematic_net_label.description: Add a net label to the schematic. PREFERRED: supply componentRef + pinNumber to snap the label to the exact pin endpoint — this guarantees an electrical connection. Alternatively supply position [x, y], but the coordinates must match the pin endpoint exactly (even a 0.01 mm offset breaks the connection). The response includes actual_position (coordinates actually used) and snapped_to_pin (present when a pin reference was resolved).

netName.description: Name of the net (e.g., VCC, GND, SIGNAL_1)

position.description: Position [x, y] for the label. Required when componentRef/pinNumber are not given.

componentRef.description: Component reference to snap label to (e.g. U1, R1). Use with pinNumber.

pinNumber.description: Pin number or name on componentRef to snap label to (e.g. '1', 'GND'). Use with componentRef.

orientation.description: Rotation angle 0/90/180/270. Omit it when snapping to a pin: the label is then oriented along the pin's outward direction so the text runs away from the symbol body instead of over it. Defaults to 0 otherwise.

add_schematic_text.name: add_schematic_text
add_schematic_text.description: Add a free-form text annotation to the schematic. Use this to add notes, labels, section headings, or documentation strings directly on the schematic canvas. Unlike net labels, text annotations have no electrical significance.

position.description: Position [x, y] in schematic mm coordinates

add_schematic_wire.name: add_schematic_wire
add_schematic_wire.description: Draws a wire on the schematic between two or more coordinate points. Always call get_schematic_pin_locations first to get the approximate pin coordinates, then pass them as the first and last waypoints. snapToPins (on by default) will correct any float imprecision by snapping endpoints to the exact nearest pin coordinate. To route around components, add intermediate waypoints between the start and end: e.g. [[x1,y1], [xMid,y1], [xMid,y2], [x2,y2]] routes horizontally then vertically. Intermediate waypoints are never snapped. The response says, for the start and end points, whether they snapped and how far the nearest pin is, and warns when an endpoint is outside snapTolerance of every pin: such a wire is floating.

waypoints.description: Ordered list of [x, y] coordinates. Minimum 2 points.

snapToPins.description: Snap the first and last waypoints to the nearest pin (default: true)

add_sheet_pin.name: add_sheet_pin
add_sheet_pin.description: Add a pin to a sheet symbol block on the parent schematic. Sheet pins are the parent-side connection points that correspond to hierarchical labels in the sub-sheet. The pinName must exactly match a hierarchical_label in the sub-sheet.

sheetName.description: Sheet name as it appears in the Sheetname property (e.g. 'Storage')

pinName.description: Pin name — must match a hierarchical_label in the sub-sheet

pinType.description: Signal direction (should match the sub-sheet hierarchical label shape)

position.description: Pin position [x, y] in mm — must be on the sheet block boundary

orientation.description: Pin orientation: 0=right edge of sheet box, 180=left edge (default: 0)

add_symbol_property.name: add_symbol_property
add_symbol_property.description: Add or update a custom property (Manufacturer, MPN, LCSC, etc.) on a symbol in a .kicad_sym library file. The property is written on the symbol itself rather than on one of its units, so multi-unit symbols are handled correctly.

position.description: Position {x, y} in mm. Omit to leave an existing property where it is (new: 0, 0)

hide.description: Hide the property. Omit to keep an existing property's visibility (new: false)

add_via.name: add_via
add_via.description: Add a via to the PCB

position.description: Via position

viaType.description: Via type. Only "through" (the default) is supported; other types are refused

add_zone.name: add_zone
add_zone.description: Create a copper zone (pour) from an explicit polygon on one or more copper layers, with priority, clearance, minimum width, pad connection (solid/thermal/none), thermal relief and island removal. Outline points use `unit` (default mm); clearance, minWidth, thermalGap and thermalSpokeWidth are mm, minIslandArea is mm². The zone is not filled until refill_zones runs. Returns {success, message, zone: {uuid, net, layers, pointCount, priority, clearance, minWidth, padConnection, ...}}.

layer.description: Copper layer for the zone, e.g. 'F.Cu'

layers.description: Several copper layers for one zone (use instead of layer), e.g. ['F.Cu','B.Cu']

net.description: Net name, exactly as on the board (hierarchical nets look like '/Power/+5V')

unit.description: Unit of the outline points (default: mm)

padConnection.description: How pads connect: thermal relief, solid, none, or thermal for THT only

thermalSpokeWidth.description: Thermal relief spoke width in mm

islandRemoval.description: Island removal mode; 'area' removes islands smaller than minIslandArea

align_components.name: align_components
align_components.description: Align multiple PCB components horizontally, vertically or on a grid with optional spacing.

references.description: Array of component references to align

annotate_schematic.name: annotate_schematic
annotate_schematic.description: Assign reference designators to unannotated components (R? → R1, R2, ...). Must be called before tools that require known references. Numbers are unique across the whole project, each use of a sheet that is placed more than once gets its own, and the units of a multi-unit part share one.

apply_property_map.name: apply_property_map
apply_property_map.description:
Bulk-set symbol fields and flags across the WHOLE schematic hierarchy from a list of rules (MCP_ISSUES S4; replaces lcsc_map-style scripts).
Each rule is {match: {value?, valueRegex?, footprint_contains?, ref_regex?, lib_id?}, set: {LCSC?: "C25804", <field>: "text", dnp?: bool, in_bom?: bool, on_board?: bool, exclude_from_sim?: bool}}.
Rules apply in order to every non-power symbol; all matching rules apply (later ones win) unless firstMatchOnly. Idempotent: values already set are not rewritten, so a second run changes nothing. All sheets are written atomically (all or none).
Returns {changedParts, changed:[{refs, sheet, changes:{field:[old,new]}}], rules:[{index, matched, refs, warning?}], unmatched:[{ref,value,footprint}] (no rule matched), missingLcsc:[...] (BOM parts, not DNP, still without an LCSC number), sheetsChanged}.

schematicPath.description: Root .kicad_sch (any sheet of the project, a .kicad_pro or project dir also works)

value.description: Exact Value field (or any of a list)

valueRegex.description: Regex that must match the whole Value

footprint_contains.description: Case-insensitive substring of the Footprint field, e.g. 'R_0603'

ref_regex.description: Regex that must match a whole reference, e.g. 'J(1|2|7)'

match.description: All given conditions must hold (AND). At least one is required.

set.description: Fields to set: any field name -> string (e.g. LCSC, MPN, Value, Footprint; 'LCSC' updates an existing 'LCSC Part #'-style field in place), plus the flags dnp, in_bom, on_board, exclude_from_sim, in_pos_files -> true/false.

dryRun.description: Report what would change without writing (default false)

firstMatchOnly.description: Apply only the first matching rule per part, like a lookup table (default false)

assert_connectivity.name: assert_connectivity
assert_connectivity.description:
Check intended pin-to-net assignments against the netlist KiCad itself exports
(kicad-cli sch export netlist, run on the project's ROOT schematic so the whole
hierarchy is included). ERC cannot see a label sitting on the wrong pin; this can.

expectations: {"U7": {"5": "+3V3", "6": "GND"}, "J1": {"S1": "GND"}} — keys are
pin numbers (pin names are accepted as a fallback). Net names match either exactly
or on their last hierarchical path component, so "+5V" matches "/Power/+5V". Use
"NC" (or null / "") for a pin that must stay unconnected.

saveAs stores the merged expectation set (by name, default "default") in
<project>/.kicad-mcp/connectivity.json; useStored re-runs a stored set (optionally
merged with new expectations), so the check can be repeated after every edit at
almost no token cost. Nothing in the design is modified.

Returns only problems: {success, passed, message, checkedPins,
mismatches:[{ref, pin, pinfunction, expected, actual}], missing:[{ref, pin?, reason}],
singlePinNets:[{net, ref, pin}] (named nets on the listed refs with one pin only),
unexpectedNoConnects:[{ref, pin, net, expected?, reason?}], rootSchematic, savedTo?}.

schematicPath.description: Any .kicad_sch of the project; the project's root schematic is used for the netlist

projectPath.description: Alternative to schematicPath: the .kicad_pro file or the project directory

expectations.description: Map of reference -> {pin: expectedNet}; "NC" or null = must be unconnected

saveAs.description: Store the expectation set under this name in <project>/.kicad-mcp/connectivity.json

useStored.description: Load the stored expectation set with this name (merged with expectations)

assign_net_to_class.name: assign_net_to_class
assign_net_to_class.description: Assign a net to an existing net class to apply its specific design rules.

autoplace_schematic_fields.name: autoplace_schematic_fields
autoplace_schematic_fields.description: Automatically reposition every component's Reference and Value field so they sit outside the component body AND outside any net labels attached to its pins, avoiding collisions with other components and already-placed fields. Like KiCAD's built-in field auto-placement but net-label aware. Optionally limit to specific references.

references.description: Only reposition these references (default: all components)

clearance.description: Gap in mm between the body/label extent and field text (default one 1.27mm grid unit)

autoroute.name: autoroute
autoroute.description: Run Freerouting autorouter on the current PCB. Exports to Specctra DSN, runs Freerouting CLI, and imports the routed SES result. Requires freerouting.jar and the Java version it was built for (21+; Freerouting 2.4.x needs 25), or Docker/Podman (see check_freerouting). Set `attempts` > 1 to run best-of-N: Freerouting is invoked multiple times with varied `--max-passes`, each result is scored by (nets_routed * 1000 + segments, +50000 bonus when every `targetNets` entry routed), and the winning SES is imported. Single-attempt behaviour is unchanged when `attempts` is omitted. Orchestrated mode (any of async, nets, lockExisting, stripRuleAreas, forbidRegionsForNets, passes, stallTimeout, importMode, evaluate, lockRouted): the in-memory board is staged to a temp copy, the DSN is exported from that disk copy and rewritten (pour-only keepouts stripped, subset/locking), Freerouting's log is streamed (stall detection), the SES is imported into a copy, zones are refilled and KiCad DRC evaluates it; the board file is replaced only if accepted (importMode) and unchanged since the start. Returns {pipeline:'orchestrated', freerouting:{attempts:[{unroutedReportedByFreerouting, stopReason,...}]}, kicad:{before:{unconnected, unconnectedByNet, drcErrors}, after:{...}}, drcDelta:{newCount, resolvedCount, new, resolved}, decision:{import, reason}, applied, logTail, dsn:{ruleAreas, netFilter, lockedWiring}} or, with async, {jobId}.

freeroutingJar.description: Path to freerouting.jar (default: ~/.kicad-mcp/freerouting.jar or FREEROUTING_JAR env)

maxPasses.description: Maximum routing passes for single-attempt mode (default: 20). Ignored when `attempts` > 1; use `passSchedule` instead.

attempts.description: Number of Freerouting runs to try (default: 1 — backward-compatible). When > 1, runs best-of-N: scores each attempt by routing completeness and keeps the SES with the highest score. Recommended: 3–5 for dense boards.

targetNets.description: Optional list of critical net names. An attempt that routes all of them earns a 50,000-point scoring bonus, breaking ties in favour of designs that include the must-have nets.

passSchedule.description: Per-attempt `--max-passes` values to cycle through (default: [50, 60, 65, 70, 75, 80, 85, 90, 55, 95]). The list wraps if `attempts` exceeds its length.

keepArtifacts.description: Keep the intermediate .dsn/.ses files next to the board after the run (default: false). Artifacts are staged in a temporary directory and removed on every exit — success, failure, or crash — unless this is set.

async.description: Run in the background and return {jobId} at once; poll job_status, then call job_apply to write an accepted result. The board is unchanged until job_apply.

nets.description: Route only these nets. Other nets keep their pads and copper as fixed obstacles, and only these nets' routing is imported.

lockExisting.description: Export all existing tracks/vias as fixed so Freerouting cannot move or rip them up (default false). Lock flags on the board are restored after import.

stripRuleAreas.description: Remove rule-area keepouts from the DSN (the board keeps them). 'pour_only' (default): rule areas that only forbid pours, which KiCad otherwise exports as hard obstacles; 'all': every rule area; 'none'.

forbidRegionsForNets.description: Keep these nets out of a region. When every routed net is listed the region becomes a hard keepout in the DSN; otherwise a listed net whose new copper enters the region is not imported (reported in forbiddenRegionRejected).

passes.description: Freerouting max passes (-mp) for the orchestrated run (default maxPasses or 20)

stallTimeout.description: Stop an attempt that makes no progress (no better pass score, no fewer unrouted, no new stage) for this many seconds. Freerouting writes no SES when stopped.

importMode.description: 'if_better' (default): import only when KiCad's own unconnected count drops without more DRC errors (or errors drop at equal count); 'always': import any result.

evaluate.description: Run kicad-cli DRC (zones refilled) before and after to report KiCad's unconnected count and the DRC delta (default true)

lockRouted.description: Lock the newly routed tracks/vias (default false)

backannotate_footprints.name: backannotate_footprints
backannotate_footprints.description: Copy footprint assignments from a .kicad_pcb back into the schematic's Footprint fields — the reverse of sync_schematic_to_board. After a layout pass the board is the side that is right: footprints get swapped in pcbnew, and imported projects land with schematic-side fields that never matched the placed parts. Matching is by reference designator, taken from each symbol's (instances ...) block so a sheet placed more than once contributes all of its designators; virtual references starting with '#' (power, ground) are skipped, and every unit of a multi-unit symbol is updated. Only the quoted value is rewritten, so field visibility, font and position survive. Ambiguous cases are reported under 'conflicts' and left unwritten; footprints with no matching symbol under 'notInSchematic'.

boardPath.description: Absolute path to the .kicad_pcb board file

schematicPath.description: Single sheet to update. Omit to walk the sheet tree from the root schematic named after the board, which is what a hierarchical design needs; local history, backup copies and other projects under the same directory are left alone.

references.description: Limit the update to these reference designators

addMissing.description: Add a Footprint field to instances that have none (default true)

dryRun.description: Report the changes without writing them

batch_add_and_connect.name: batch_add_and_connect
batch_add_and_connect.description: Place multiple components AND wire their nets in a single call — the fewest-round-trip way to build a subcircuit. Each component is like batch_add_components plus an optional 'nets' map {pin: netName}. Components are placed first, then nets are connected via batch_connect. labelType selects 'label' (sheet-local, default) or 'global_label' (cross-sheet by name) for all the nets wired in this call.

nets.description: Map of pin -> netName to label after placement

labelType.description: Label kind used to wire the nets: 'label' = sheet-local (default); 'global_label' = cross-sheet by name

scope.description: Label scope, overrides labelType: 'local' = label, 'global' = global_label, 'auto' = per net, a global label when the net name is already used on another sheet of the hierarchy (or as a global label on this sheet), else a local label. Omit to use labelType.

batch_add_components.name: batch_add_components
batch_add_components.description: Add multiple components to a schematic in one call (far fewer round-trips than add_schematic_component). Each component: {symbol:'Library:Name', reference, value?, footprint?, position:{x,y}, rotation?, includePins?, unit?}. Multi-unit parts are placed one entry per unit, sharing a reference. Reference/Value fields are auto-positioned outside the body (disable with auto_position_fields=false). Returns per-component snapped position, field positions, body_bbox, and an overall placement_bbox.

unit.description: Unit of a multi-unit part (1=A, 2=B, …), default 1. Place each unit as its own entry, all sharing the same reference.

origin_x.description: X offset added to every component position (mm)

origin_y.description: Y offset added to every component position (mm)

auto_position_fields.description: Auto-place Ref/Value fields outside the body (default true)

batch_add_no_connects.name: batch_add_no_connects
batch_add_no_connects.description: Add no-connect (X) flags to multiple pins in one call, to mark intentionally unconnected pins and silence ERC. 'pins' is a list of {componentRef, pinName}.

batch_connect.name: batch_connect
batch_connect.description: Place net labels on multiple pins in one call to wire nets quickly. 'connections' is a map {reference: {pin: netName}} where pin is a number or name. labelType selects 'label' (sheet-local, the default) or 'global_label' (connects across all sheets by name — use this for power rails and any net that spans sheets). For local labels, if a facing label for the same net is nearby an orthogonal wire (straight, or a Z with a grid-snapped jog — never diagonal) is drawn instead of a duplicate label; when that wire would land on or cross another object a plain label is placed instead. Global labels are placed one-per-pin since they join their net by name. On two-pin parts a label whose text would overlap a visible Reference/Value field is moved 2.54 or 5.08 mm out along the pin with a stub wire (avoidFieldOverlap, default true). scope='auto' picks global_label per net when the name is already used on another sheet of the hierarchy, else a local label (each placed row then reports labelType). Set replace=true to remove every existing label (local, global, hierarchical) on each pin first, plus a wire run from the pin that ends at a label of another net (e.g. an earlier auto-wire to another pin's label) when nothing else hangs off it. Coordinates are schematic mm, origin top-left, Y down. Returns {success, message, placed:[{ref, pin, net, position:{x,y}, label_position?, wire?, note?, replaced?}], failed:[{ref, pin, reason}], warnings?}. Warns only about nets touched by this call that hold a power_in pin and no power_out pin (PWR_FLAG or regulator output) anywhere in the sheet hierarchy.

labelType.description: Label kind: 'label' = sheet-local (default); 'global_label' = connects across all sheets by name

scope.description: Label scope, overrides labelType: 'local' = label, 'global' = global_label, 'auto' = per net, a global label when the net name is already used on another sheet of the hierarchy (or as a global label on this sheet), else a local label. Omit to use labelType.

replace.description: Delete every existing label (local, global, hierarchical) at each pin, a label at the end of a bare stub from it, and a branch-free wire run from the pin to another net's label, before placing (default false)

avoidFieldOverlap.description: On two-pin parts, move a label out along the pin (with a stub wire) when its text would overlap a visible Reference/Value field (default true)

batch_edit_schematic_components.name: batch_edit_schematic_components
batch_edit_schematic_components.description: Edit multiple existing components in one call. 'components' is a map {reference: {value?, footprint?, newReference?, ...}}; each entry is applied via the single-component editor. Returns per-reference updated/errors.

components.description: Map of reference -> fields to change

batch_list_symbol_pins.name: batch_list_symbol_pins
batch_list_symbol_pins.description: Return pin names, numbers, types, and symbol-local coordinates for multiple symbols in a single call. Use instead of calling list_symbol_pins repeatedly when placing a subcircuit — saves 5–10 round-trips. Each result includes pins (with x/y/angle in symbol-local coords, Y-up per KiCAD lib convention) and body_bbox (bounding box of pin envelope ±1.27mm, symbol-local coords). IMPORTANT: coordinates are symbol-local (Y-up, pre-rotation); after placement use get_schematic_pin_locations for post-rotation schematic coordinates. Set compact=true for simple 2-pin passives (Device:R/C/L) to get just pin_count, body_bbox, and is_symmetric.

schematicPath.description: Path to .kicad_sch — enables project-local sym-lib-table lookup

compact.description: If true, omit per-pin detail for standard 2-pin symmetric passives.

batch_move_components.name: batch_move_components
batch_move_components.description: Move multiple PCB components transactionally. If one reference/spec is invalid, no components are moved. Saves by default unless save=false.

moves.description: Map of reference designator to placement spec

save.description: Save the board after all moves succeed (default true)

dryRun.description: Validate the batch without changing the board

batch_set_schematic_property_positions.name: batch_set_schematic_property_positions
batch_set_schematic_property_positions.description: Move many Reference/Value field labels in a single file read/write — far faster than repeated set_schematic_property_position calls. Pass an 'updates' array; each item is {reference, property:'Reference'|'Value', x, y, angle?, visible?}. Returns per-item applied/failed lists.

updates.description: List of field moves to apply

calculate_impedance.name: calculate_impedance
calculate_impedance.description: Estimate controlled impedance on a copper layer from the board stackup, or solve the trace width (or pair gap) for a target. Outer layers are surface microstrip (Hammerstad-Jensen; edge-coupled pairs Kirschning-Jansen), inner layers stripline between the adjacent copper layers (Wheeler; pairs Cohn), offset when the two dielectric heights differ. Returns Z0, or Zdiff/Zodd/Zeven/Zcommon, with the stackup geometry used, the model, and an accuracy note (about +/-5% of a field solver; solder mask, etch and dispersion not modelled). A board without a stackup falls back to a JLC-like 1.6 mm default and says so. Read-only.

layer.description: Copper layer of the trace, e.g. F.Cu or In2.Cu

mode.description: single-ended trace or edge-coupled pair. Defaults to differential when gap or targetDiffImpedance is given

width.description: Trace width in mm. Kept fixed when solving a pair's gap

gap.description: Edge-to-edge gap of the pair in mm. Kept fixed when solving the width (default 0.2)

targetImpedance.description: Single-ended Z0 target in ohms (mode single); solves the width

targetDiffImpedance.description: Differential target in ohms (mode differential), e.g. 90 USB, 100 Ethernet/LVDS. Solves the gap when only width is given, otherwise the width

minWidth.description: Smallest width the solver may return, mm (default: the board's minimum track width, else 0.05)

maxWidth.description: Largest width the solver may return, mm (default 5)

minGap.description: Smallest gap the solver may return, mm (default: the board's minimum clearance, else 0.05)

maxGap.description: Largest gap the solver may return, mm (default 5)

referenceLayers.description: Copper layers that are solid reference planes. Default: the copper layers directly above and below the trace layer

check_clearance.name: check_clearance
check_clearance.description: Check the actual clearance between two PCB items (track, via, pad, zone or component) and report whether it meets the design rules.

id.description: ID of the first item (if applicable)

position.description: Position to check (if ID not provided)

id.description: ID of the second item (if applicable)

position.description: Position to check (if ID not provided)

check_courtyard_overlaps.name: check_courtyard_overlaps
check_courtyard_overlaps.description: Detect courtyard overlaps between footprints and (optionally) flag courtyards that extend past the board outline. Accepts a `positions` dict of hypothetical placements so an AI can validate a proposed move_component / place_component before committing it. Returns overlap pairs with intersection extents (mm) and per-component boundary violations.

positions.description: Virtual placements: map of reference designator to [x, y] or [x, y, rotation_degrees] in mm. Each listed ref is checked AS IF it were at the given coordinates. Unspecified refs use their current board position.

refs.description: Limit the check to these refs (default: every footprint on the board).

margin.description: Extra clearance in mm added around every courtyard (default 0). Useful to enforce a manufacturing keepout wider than the symbol's declared courtyard.

include_boundary.description: Also flag courtyards that extend past the board outline (default true).

board_outline.description: Optional board outline bbox override. Default: derived from Edge.Cuts.

check_freerouting.name: check_freerouting
check_freerouting.description: Check if Java and Freerouting JAR are available on the system. Run this before autoroute to verify prerequisites.

check_kicad_ui.name: check_kicad_ui
check_kicad_ui.description: Check if KiCAD UI is currently running

check_placement_clearance.name: check_placement_clearance
check_placement_clearance.description: Classify placement conflicts as body overlap, courtyard overlap, keepout violation, silk/text overlap or pad clearance.

margin.description: Extra bbox margin in mm for mechanical checks

padClearance.description: Extra pad bbox clearance in mm

check_standards.name: check_standards
check_standards.description: Check the board against the project's standards profile (standards.yaml/.yml/.json next to the project; MCP_ISSUES §2.9): fab minimums (track, drill, annular ring, silkscreen, board rules looser than the fab), region intrusion (allowed_nets/forbidden_nets, forbid_regions), plane-split crossings for no_plane_split_crossing classes (from the zones on the plane layers), class width and preferred layer, GND SMD pads without a nearby via, exposed pads without vias, decoupling distance. Compact like run_drc: counts, first `limit` items, and a delta against the previous check. run_drc appends the same summary when a profile exists.

profilePath.description: Profile file (default: found next to the project)

profile.description: Inline profile object (same shape as the file)

projectPath.description: Project directory or .kicad_pro to look in

checks.description: Run only these: fab, regions, netclasses, or a checks: key such as decoupling_within_mm

record.description: Record this run as the baseline for the next delta (default true)

limit.description: Max items listed (default 20)

cleanup_dangling.name: cleanup_dangling
cleanup_dangling.description: Trim dangling track stubs back to their last junction (pad, via, track or zone contact) instead of deleting whole segments, repeating along a stub chain, and remove vias that connect to nothing or only to one stub track (stitching vias inside a same-net zone are kept). Dangling ends are the ones KiCad's DRC reports (track_dangling). The result is checked against KiCad connectivity: if any net has more separate pad groups or the unconnected count rose, every change is rolled back (success=false, rolledBack=true). Units mm. Returns {removedTracks, trimmedTracks, removedVias, unresolved, connectivity:{unconnectedBefore,unconnectedAfter,netsWorse}, actions (first `limit`), saved}.

region.description: Only items with a point inside this rectangle (mm)

limit.description: Max actions listed in the reply (default 50)

dryRun.description: Report what would change without changing the board

clear_board_outline.name: clear_board_outline
clear_board_outline.description: Delete all Edge.Cuts graphics from the current PCB board.

close_project.name: close_project
close_project.description: Close the currently loaded KiCAD project: optionally save, then drop the in-memory board and clear session state. Use this to hand control back so the user (or the agent) can edit project files directly without the MCP later clobbering those changes on save.

save.description: Save the board to disk before closing (default true). If false and there are unsaved changes, the close proceeds but the response warns they were discarded.

forceExternalChanges.description: Save despite external changes to the loaded SWIG board file

connect_passthrough.name: connect_passthrough
connect_passthrough.description: Connects all pins of a source connector (e.g. J1) to matching pins of a target connector (e.g. J2) via shared net labels — pin N gets net '{netPrefix}_{N}'. Use this for FFC/ribbon cable passthrough adapters instead of calling connect_to_net for every pin.

netPrefix.description: Net name prefix, e.g. 'CSI' → CSI_1, CSI_2 (default: PIN)

pinOffset.description: Add to pin number when building net name (default: 0)

connect_to_net.name: connect_to_net
connect_to_net.description: Connect a component pin to a named net by adding a wire stub and net label at the exact pin endpoint. The response includes pin_location (exact pin coords), label_location (where the label was placed), and wire_stub (the wire segment added) so you can confirm the placement. scope selects the label kind (default 'local'; 'auto' = global when the net name is already used on another sheet); the response's label_type says which was placed.

netName.description: Name of the net to connect to

scope.description: 'local' = label (default), 'global' = global_label, 'auto' = global_label when the net name is already used on another sheet of the hierarchy, else a local label

connected_items.name: connected_items
connected_items.description: Find the copper island an item or a point belongs to, using KiCad's connectivity engine. Start from uuid (full or a unique prefix of 8+ characters, as query_region shows), ref + pad, or x + y (optionally layer; a point picks pad > via > track > zone fill). Units: mm, KiCad board coordinates (absolute positions as stored in the .kicad_pcb, +y down; not relative to a grid or aux origin). Returns {start, otherHits?, net, netIslandCount, isWholeNet, island:{island, pads, tracks, vias, zoneFills, layers, bbox, padList}}; detail "items"/"full" adds the island's items as query_region-style rows. If netIslandCount > 1 the net is split: call why_unconnected for the gaps.

uuid.description: Pad, track, via or zone uuid (or unique prefix, >= 8 chars)

layer.description: Copper layer for the point (and to pick a zone layer)

detail.description: summary (default) = island summary; items/full = also list the island's items

limit.description: Maximum rows / pads listed (default 40)

boardPath.description: Absolute path to a .kicad_pcb to read fresh from disk. Omit to use the board loaded in memory (unsaved edits included).

copy_routing_pattern.name: copy_routing_pattern
copy_routing_pattern.description: Copy routing pattern (traces and vias) from a group of source components to a matching group of target components. The offset is calculated automatically from the position difference between the first source and first target component. Useful for replicating routing between identical circuit blocks.

targetRefs.description: References of the target components in same order as sourceRefs (e.g. ['U2', 'R2', 'C2'])

traceWidth.description: Override trace width in mm (default: keep original width)

create_board_from_schematic.name: create_board_from_schematic
create_board_from_schematic.description: Create a new .kicad_pcb file from a schematic, then update the PCB from that schematic so footprints and nets are present.

schematicPath.description: Absolute path to the .kicad_sch schematic file

boardPath.description: Destination .kicad_pcb path; defaults next to schematic

overwrite.description: Replace boardPath if it already exists

create_footprint.name: create_footprint
create_footprint.description: Create a new KiCAD footprint (.kicad_mod) inside a .pretty library directory. Supports SMD and THT pads, courtyard, silkscreen, and fab-layer rectangles.

libraryPath.description: Path to the .pretty library directory (created if missing). E.g. C:/MyProject/MyLib.pretty

shape.description: Pad shape (default: rect for SMD, circle for THT)

roundrect_ratio.description: Corner radius ratio for roundrect shape (0.0–0.5, default 0.25)

pads.description: List of pads to add (can be empty for outlines-only footprints)

courtyard.description: Courtyard rectangle on F.CrtYd (recommended: 0.25 mm clearance around pads)

fabLayer.description: Fab-layer rectangle on F.Fab (shows component body)

create_hierarchical_subsheet.name: create_hierarchical_subsheet
create_hierarchical_subsheet.description: Create a new sub-sheet .kicad_sch file and link it into a parent schematic in a single call (create_schematic + add_hierarchical_sheet). The fastest way to grow a hierarchical design.

subsheetPath.description: Path for the new sub-sheet .kicad_sch to create

metadata.description: Optional metadata for the new sub-sheet (title, etc.)

create_netclass.name: create_netclass
create_netclass.description: Create or update a net class (sizes in mm) and assign nets to it. Each entry of nets/patterns is written to the project's net_settings.netclass_patterns and checked against the board: nets on a sub-sheet carry the sheet path (e.g. '/Power/+5V', not '+5V'). Returns {success, netClass: {name, nets, trackWidth, clearance, ..., unit: 'mm'}, assignments: [{pattern, matchedNets, matchCount, suggestions?}], persisted, patternsPersisted, appliedInMemory, warnings?}; a pattern that matches no net is reported in warnings.

uviaDrill.description: Micro via drill size in mm

diffPairWidth.description: Differential pair trace width in mm

nets.description: Exact board net names to assign to this class, e.g. ['/Power/+5V','GND']

patterns.description: KiCad netclass patterns with * and ? wildcards, e.g. ['/Power/*', 'VBUS*']

create_symbol.name: create_symbol
create_symbol.description:
Create a new schematic symbol in a .kicad_sym library file (created if missing). After creation, use register_symbol_library so KiCAD finds it. Pin positions are where the wire connects; the symbol body is drawn between them.

Coordinate tips:
- Body rectangle typically spans ±2.54 to ±5.08 mm
- Pins on left side: at.x = body_left - length, angle=0 (wire goes right)
- Pins on right side: at.x = body_right + length, angle=180 (wire goes left)
- Pins on top: at.y = body_top + length, angle=270 (wire goes down)
- Pins on bottom: at.y = body_bottom - length, angle=90 (wire goes up)
- Standard pin length: 2.54 mm, standard grid: 2.54 mm

libraryPath.description: Path to the .kicad_sym file (created if missing)

onBoard.description: Include in netlist for PCB (default true)

angle.description: Direction the pin wire extends FROM the symbol body: 0=right, 90=up, 180=left, 270=down

at.description: Pin endpoint position (where the wire connects)

pins.description: List of pins (can be empty for graphical-only symbols)

rectangles.description: Body rectangle(s). Typically one rectangle defining the IC body.

points.description: List of XY points in mm

polylines.description: Polyline graphics for custom body shapes (op-amp triangles, etc.)

overwrite.description: Replace existing symbol with same name (default false)

delete_component.name: delete_component
delete_component.description: Remove a component from the PCB by its reference designator.

reference.description: Reference designator of the component to delete (e.g., 'R5')

delete_graphic.name: delete_graphic
delete_graphic.description: Delete a PCB graphic/drawing item by UUID.

uuid.description: KiCad UUID of the graphic item

delete_schematic_component.name: delete_schematic_component
delete_schematic_component.description:
Remove a placed symbol from a KiCAD schematic (.kicad_sch).

This removes the symbol instance (the placed component) from the schematic.
It does NOT remove the symbol definition from lib_symbols.

With deleteAttachedLabels, net labels sitting exactly on the deleted
component's pin positions are removed too — unless a label is still attached
to a wire or another component's pin. Recommended when permanently removing
a wired part, since orphaned labels otherwise produce label_dangling ERC
errors. Default false for backward compatibility (delete-then-re-add
workflows rely on labels surviving).

deleteAttachedWires (defaults to deleteAttachedLabels) also trims wires left
dangling at the deleted pins, e.g. an auto-drawn wire from a PWR_FLAG. A wire is
removed only when its end sits on a deleted pin with nothing else there; the
trim continues through bare corners and stops at the first junction, pin, label
or sheet pin, so wires that still connect other things are kept. A label left
floating at the far end of a removed stub is removed with the label pass.
Returns {success, reference, deleted_count, deleted_labels?, deleted_wires?
[{start:{x,y}, end:{x,y}}] (mm), ...}.

Note: This tool operates on schematic files (.kicad_sch).
To remove a footprint from a PCB, use delete_component instead.

reference.description: Reference designator of the component to remove (e.g. R1, U3)

deleteAttachedLabels.description: Also delete net labels sitting on the deleted component's pin positions, unless still attached to a wire or another component's pin (default false)

deleteAttachedWires.description: Also trim wires left dangling at the deleted pins, back to the first junction, pin, label or sheet pin (default: same as deleteAttachedLabels)

unit.description: Unit of a multi-unit part (1=A, 2=B, …) to remove. Every unit shares one reference, so without this ALL units of the part are deleted.

delete_schematic_net_label.name: delete_schematic_net_label
delete_schematic_net_label.description: Remove a net label from the schematic.

netName.description: Name of the net label to remove

position.description: Position to disambiguate if multiple labels with same name

delete_schematic_wire.name: delete_schematic_wire
delete_schematic_wire.description: Remove a wire from the schematic by start and end coordinates.

delete_symbol.name: delete_symbol
delete_symbol.description: Remove a symbol from a .kicad_sym library file.

delete_trace.name: delete_trace
delete_trace.description: Delete traces from the PCB. Can delete by UUID, position, or bulk-delete all traces on a net.

traceUuid.description: UUID of a specific trace to delete

position.description: Delete trace nearest to this position

net.description: Delete all traces on this net (bulk delete)

layer.description: Filter by layer when using net-based deletion

diff_snapshots.name: diff_snapshots
diff_snapshots.description:
Compare two snapshots, or a snapshot with the current files (MCP_ISSUES I1). Read-only.
Board: footprints added/removed/moved (dx, dy in mm, drot in degrees, layer) and value/footprint changes, track and via count deltas per net (with track length delta in mm), zones and rule areas added/removed/reshaped. Schematic: symbols added/removed and changed fields/flags by reference, label/wire/junction count deltas per sheet. Also lists files added/removed/modified.
Returns {a, b, files[], board:{footprints, tracks, vias, zones}, schematic:{symbols, sheets}}.

b.description: Newer snapshot, or 'current' for the files on disk (default)

projectPath.description: Project directory or any project file (default: the loaded board's)

limit.description: Max items per list (default 50)

digikey_check_library_availability.name: digikey_check_library_availability
digikey_check_library_availability.description: Look up every symbol in a .kicad_sym on Digi-Key and report which parts are obsolete, out of stock, unfindable, or missing a part number altogether — the check to run before a board goes to purchasing, and after inheriting a library from an import. Each symbol is searched by its distributor part number first and its manufacturer part number second, because retired Digi-Key numbers are the common failure and the MPN usually still resolves; searchByMpnFirst reverses that. Part numbers are read under any of the property spellings real libraries use (MPN, MP, 'MANUFACTURER PART NUMBER', 'PART NUMBER', 'SUPPLIER PART NUMBER 1'). Budget up to two rate-limited requests per symbol — the fallback costs a second one whenever the first term misses — plus one token request, so raise maxSymbols deliberately.

libraryPath.description: Absolute path to the .kicad_sym library file

symbols.description: Only check these symbol names (default: every symbol in the library)

maxSymbols.description: Stop after this many symbols (default 25). Each symbol costs one or two rate-limited API requests and the client throttles itself between them, so a larger sweep takes minutes; raising this past a few hundred will exhaust even the extended timeout this tool runs under.

searchByMpnFirst.description: Search by manufacturer part number before the distributor number

site.description: Digi-Key site, e.g. US, DE, UK

locale.description: Override the locale for this call. Digi-Key requires locale headers on every request — without them a search returns 404 — but the values are yours to pick. Defaults come from DIGIKEY_LOCALE_* or US/en/USD. Note the response is localized too, so the lifecycle status and the packaging names come back in the language you ask for; the tools compare ids rather than those strings.

digikey_search_parts.name: digikey_search_parts
digikey_search_parts.description: Search Digi-Key by part number, manufacturer part number, or a parametric phrase ('0402 100nF 50V X7R'), returning stock, price, lifecycle status, packaging variations and the parametric table. Two details the raw API makes easy to get wrong are handled here: the Digi-Key part number lives on each packaging variation rather than on the product, so reel and cut tape have different numbers; and lifecycle is read from ProductStatus.Id rather than the status string, which is localized. Use preferPackaging to pick which variation is quoted as the headline part number.

keywords.description: Part number, MPN, or a parametric phrase such as '0402 100nF 50V X7R'

limit.description: Results to return, 1-50 (default 10)

preferPackaging.description: Which packaging variation to quote as the headline part number: TR (tape & reel, production), CT (cut tape, prototypes), DKR (Digi-Reel). Matching handles localized packaging names.

site.description: Digi-Key site, e.g. US, DE, UK

locale.description: Override the locale for this call. Digi-Key requires locale headers on every request — without them a search returns 404 — but the values are yours to pick. Defaults come from DIGIKEY_LOCALE_* or US/en/USD. Note the response is localized too, so the lifecycle status and the packaging names come back in the language you ask for; the tools compare ids rather than those strings.

digikey_test_connection.name: digikey_test_connection
digikey_test_connection.description: Verify that the server's Digi-Key credentials work: fetch a token and run one search. Use this first when a Digi-Key tool reports an authentication problem, since it distinguishes missing credentials from rejected ones from a locale misconfiguration. Credentials come from DIGIKEY_CLIENT_ID and DIGIKEY_CLIENT_SECRET in the server environment; they are never accepted as arguments and never appear in a response.

site.description: Digi-Key site, e.g. US, DE, UK

locale.description: Override the locale for this call. Digi-Key requires locale headers on every request — without them a search returns 404 — but the values are yours to pick. Defaults come from DIGIKEY_LOCALE_* or US/en/USD. Note the response is localized too, so the lifecycle status and the packaging names come back in the language you ask for; the tools compare ids rather than those strings.

discard_or_reload.name: discard_or_reload
discard_or_reload.description: Discard the current in-memory PCB state and reload the board from disk.

boardPath.description: Optional .kicad_pcb path; defaults to current board

download_jlcpcb_database.name: download_jlcpcb_database
download_jlcpcb_database.description:
Download the JLCPCB parts catalog to a local SQLite database for fast offline search.

Sources (no API credentials required by default):
  - cdfer (default): in-stock subset (~480k parts, ~400 MB download). Single file,
    no extra tools — the most reliable path, especially on Windows.
  - yaqwsx: the FULL catalog (all parts incl. out-of-stock, ~2.9M parts, ~230 MB download).
    Use source="yaqwsx" if you specifically want everything. Requires a 7z CLI.
  - official: official JLCPCB API, used only if JLCPCB_APP_ID/JLCPCB_API_KEY/
    JLCPCB_API_SECRET are set.

One-time setup; downloads resume automatically if interrupted. Re-run with
force=true to refresh.

force.description: Force re-download even if database exists

source.description: Force one source. "cdfer" (default) = in-stock subset, no 7z needed. "yaqwsx" = FULL catalog, ~2.9M parts (needs a 7z CLI). "official" = JLCPCB API (needs creds).

duplicate_component.name: duplicate_component
duplicate_component.description: Duplicate an existing PCB component at an offset position, optionally with a new reference designator.

edit_component.name: edit_component
edit_component.description: Edit properties of an existing PCB component (reference, value, footprint).

edit_footprint_pad.name: edit_footprint_pad
edit_footprint_pad.description: Edit an existing pad inside a .kicad_mod footprint file. Updates size, position, drill, or shape without recreating the whole footprint.

footprintPath.description: Full path to the .kicad_mod file, e.g. C:/MyLib.pretty/R_Custom.kicad_mod

padNumber.description: Pad number to edit, e.g. '1' or 2

edit_schematic_component.name: edit_schematic_component
edit_schematic_component.description:
Update properties of a placed symbol in a KiCAD schematic (.kicad_sch) in-place.

Use this tool to:
  • assign or update the footprint, value, or reference designator,
  • reposition field labels (Reference / Value text),
  • add, update, or remove ARBITRARY CUSTOM PROPERTIES used by BOM and sourcing
    workflows: MPN, Manufacturer, Manufacturer_PN, Distributor, DigiKey, DigiKey_PN,
    Mouser_PN, LCSC, JLCPCB_PN, Voltage, Tolerance, Power, Dielectric, etc.

Custom properties are first-class — they survive ERC, are exported by export_bom,
and are picked up by the JLCPCB / Digi-Key BOM tooling. Newly-added properties
default to hidden so they do not clutter the schematic canvas.

Multiple updates can be batched in a single call: pass any combination of
`footprint`, `value`, `newReference`, `fieldPositions`, `properties`,
and `removeProperties` together.

This is more efficient than delete + re-add because it preserves the component's
position and UUID. Operates on .kicad_sch files only — to modify a PCB footprint
use edit_component instead.

reference.description: Current reference designator of the component (e.g. R1, U3)

Exposed (centre) pads get a via grid instead; fine-pitch pins are skipped. Every site is checked against all other-net copper (with the project's net-class clearances), same-net drills, the board edge, rule areas that forbid vias/tracks, optional courtyards, and the vias placed earlier in the run. regionPolicy 'zone' (default) only places a via where it lands in a same-net zone on another layer. All units mm. Returns {placed:{vias,stubs,pads}, skipped:{alreadyServed,finePitch,notInPlaneRegion,noRoom,notSmd}, noRoom:["REF.PAD (NET)"], items:[{pad,net,kind:'stub'|'exposedPadGrid',via:{x,y},stub?:{from,to,width,layer}}]}. Nothing is written with dryRun; the board is unchanged on failure.
