find_duplicate_symbols.name: find_duplicate_symbols
find_duplicate_symbols.description: Group symbols in a .kicad_sym that are the same part stored twice under different names — the residue of Eagle imports, SnapEDA downloads, and parts re-added because search did not find the existing name. KiCAD reports nothing here because the names differ, which is also why grepping does not find it. Matches on manufacturer part number (tolerating the inconsistent property naming real libraries have: MPN, MP, 'MANUFACTURER PART NUMBER', 'PART NUMBER'), on distributor part number, on Value+Footprint, on an identical drawn body, or on near-identical names. Pass schematicPaths to count how many instances each duplicate actually has — that turns the report into a decision, because the one nothing places is the one to retire.

libraryPath.description: Absolute path to the .kicad_sym library file

matchBy.description: How to decide two symbols are the same part (default: mpn, value_footprint). 'graphics' is off by default: every resistor in a library shares one body, so on passives it groups the whole family.

schematicPaths.description: .kicad_sch files or directories to scan for usage counts (recursive, skipping autosave sheets and backup/history folders). Only placements of this library count, and a sub-sheet instantiated more than once counts once per instantiation.

libraryNicknames.description: The nickname(s) this library is registered under in a lib_id, if the file stem and the sym-lib-table entries beside the scanned sheets do not cover it. A bare 'R' in this library is not Device:R, so placements naming another library are not counted towards it.

minGroupSize.description: Only report groups with at least this many symbols (default 2)

ignoreCase.description: Compare part numbers and values case-insensitively (default true)

find_orphaned_wires.name: find_orphaned_wires
find_orphaned_wires.description: Find wire segments with at least one dangling endpoint — not connected to a component pin, net label, or another wire. Orphaned wires cause ERC 'wire end unconnected' errors. Does not require the KiCad UI to be running.

find_overlapping_elements.name: find_overlapping_elements
find_overlapping_elements.description: Detect spatially overlapping symbols, wires, and labels in the schematic. Finds duplicate power symbols at the same position, collinear overlapping wires, and labels stacked on top of each other.

tolerance.description: Distance threshold in mm for label proximity and wire collinearity checks. Symbol overlap uses bounding-box intersection. (default: 0.5)

find_wires_crossing_symbols.name: find_wires_crossing_symbols
find_wires_crossing_symbols.description: Find all wires that cross over component symbol bodies. Wires passing over symbols are unacceptable in schematics — they indicate routing mistakes where a wire was drawn across a component instead of around it.

generate_netlist.name: generate_netlist
generate_netlist.description: Return a structured JSON netlist from the schematic — component list (reference, value, footprint) and net list (net name with all connected component/pin pairs). Use this to inspect or verify connectivity within the conversation. Does not write any file. To export a netlist file in Spice, KiCad XML, Cadstar, or OrcadPCB2 format, use export_netlist instead.

schematicPath.description: Absolute path to the .kicad_sch schematic file

get_backend_state.name: get_backend_state
get_backend_state.description: Return the active backend, realtime status, loaded project/board paths, and dirty state.

get_board_2d_view.name: get_board_2d_view
get_board_2d_view.description: Render a 2D image of the PCB using kicad-cli. Returns PNG, JPG, or SVG. Use layers to filter — e.g. ["F.Cu","B.Cu","Edge.Cuts"] for copper + outline only. Use responseMode to choose delivery:   "inline" (default) — PNG/JPG rendered as an image visible to Claude; SVG returned as text.   "file" — image written next to the .kicad_pcb as <board>_2d_view.<ext>; filePath is returned. Use file mode for large boards to avoid MCP message-size limits. Zoom and highlight: region, scale, highlightNets, showRatsnest or showDrcMarkers switch to a native renderer (png/jpg) that draws the board from pcbnew geometry, in memory (unsaved edits included) or from pcbPath. It crops to region {x0,y0,x1,y1} (mm, KiCad board coordinates), draws highlightNets in colour with everything else grey, labels a mm grid, and returns a view legend: pixel (0,0) = (x0,y0), px = (x-x0)*pxPerMm, plus highlight colours, ratsnest gap lines and DRC markers in view.

pcbPath.description: Absolute path to the .kicad_pcb file. Falls back to the currently loaded board if omitted.

layers.description: Layer names to include, e.g. ["F.Cu","B.Cu","Edge.Cuts"]. Omit for all layers.

responseMode.description: "inline" (default): image returned directly; "file": written to disk, filePath returned

region.description: Crop window in mm (KiCad board coordinates). Default: board outline + 1 mm

scale.description: Pixels per mm (e.g. 40 for a 0.4 mm-pitch QFN). Default: fit width x height

highlightNets.description: Nets drawn in bright colours on top; everything else is greyed

showRatsnest.description: Draw the gaps between islands (unrouted connections) for highlightNets (true) or the listed nets

showDrcMarkers.description: Mark violations from the last run_drc report (<board>_drc_violations.json)

grid.description: Label a mm grid on region renders (default true)

get_board_extents.name: get_board_extents
get_board_extents.description: Return the bounding box (min/max X and Y) of all objects on the current PCB board.

unit.description: Unit of measurement for the result

get_board_info.name: get_board_info
get_board_info.description: Retrieve general information about the current PCB board (dimensions, layer count, DRC status).

get_board_origin.name: get_board_origin
get_board_origin.description: Read back the auxiliary (drill/place) origin and grid origin of a .kicad_pcb in mm.

get_component_geometry.name: get_component_geometry
get_component_geometry.description: Return separated footprint geometry bboxes: body, pads, courtyard, keepout, fab, silk and text.

get_component_list.name: get_component_list
get_component_list.description: Return a list of all components on the PCB, optionally filtered by layer or bounding box region. matchPadCenter also keeps a footprint when any pad centre is inside the box. includePads adds each pad's number, net, and position.

layer.description: Filter by layer (e.g., 'F.Cu', 'B.Cu')

boundingBox.description: Filter by bounding box region. The footprint anchor must lie inside

matchPadCenter.description: With boundingBox, also include a footprint when any pad centre is inside, even if the anchor is outside

includePads.description: Add each footprint's pads with number, net, and position in millimetres

get_component_pads.name: get_component_pads
get_component_pads.description: Return all pads of a PCB component with their positions, net assignments and sizes.

get_component_properties.name: get_component_properties
get_component_properties.description: Return all properties of a PCB component (position, rotation, layer, value, footprint).

get_datasheet_url.name: get_datasheet_url
get_datasheet_url.description:
Get the LCSC datasheet URL for a component by LCSC number.

Returns the direct PDF URL and product page URL.
No network request – URL is constructed from the LCSC number alone.

Example: get_datasheet_url("C179739")
→ https://www.lcsc.com/datasheet/C179739.pdf

lcsc.description: LCSC part number, with or without "C" prefix (e.g. "C179739" or "179739")

get_design_rules.name: get_design_rules
get_design_rules.description: Return the current PCB design rules (clearance, track width, via sizes, courtyard settings).

get_drc_violations.name: get_drc_violations
get_drc_violations.description: Return the list of current DRC violations on the PCB, optionally filtered by severity (error, warning).

get_elements_in_region.name: get_elements_in_region
get_elements_in_region.description: List all symbols, wires, and labels within a rectangular region of the schematic. Useful for understanding what is in a specific area before modifying it.

x1.description: Left X coordinate of the region in mm

y1.description: Top Y coordinate of the region in mm

x2.description: Right X coordinate of the region in mm

y2.description: Bottom Y coordinate of the region in mm

get_footprint_info.name: get_footprint_info
get_footprint_info.description: Get detailed information about a specific footprint

library_name.description: Name of the library containing the footprint

footprint_name.description: Name of the footprint to get information about

get_jlcpcb_database_stats.name: get_jlcpcb_database_stats
get_jlcpcb_database_stats.description: Get statistics about the local JLCPCB parts database

get_jlcpcb_part.name: get_jlcpcb_part
get_jlcpcb_part.description:
Get detailed information about a specific JLCPCB part by LCSC number.

When JLCPCB Open Platform credentials are configured (JLCPCB_APP_ID / JLCPCB_API_KEY /
JLCPCB_API_SECRET, e.g. in a project-root .env), this performs a REAL-TIME lookup — live
stock, tiered pricing, parameters and library type — and falls back to the local snapshot
database if the API call fails or no credentials are set. The response reports which backend
answered via "source" ("live-api" vs "local-db").

get_layer_list.name: get_layer_list
get_layer_list.description: Return the list of all layers defined in the current PCB board.

get_net_at_point.name: get_net_at_point
get_net_at_point.description: Returns the net name at a given (x, y) coordinate in a schematic, or null if no net label or wire endpoint is present at that position. Faster than get_wire_connections when you only need the net name at a known coordinate and don't need pin traversal.

get_net_connections.name: get_net_connections
get_net_connections.description: Get all connections for a named net

netName.description: Name of the net to query

get_net_pads.name: get_net_pads
get_net_pads.description: Return every PCB pad attached to a net name or net code.

get_nets_list.name: get_nets_list
get_nets_list.description: Get a list of all nets in the PCB with optional statistics.

includeStats.description: Add per-net stats: track count, total track length and via count

get_pad_position.name: get_pad_position
get_pad_position.description: Return the exact XY position of a specific pad on a PCB component. Use this before routing to get accurate start/end coordinates.

get_pads.name: get_pads
get_pads.description: Return pads for one PCB component, selected refs, or all components, including XY, layer, size and net.

get_project_info.name: get_project_info
get_project_info.description: Get information about the current KiCAD project

get_ratsnest.name: get_ratsnest
get_ratsnest.description: Estimate ratsnest/airwire segments and lengths from current pad positions grouped by net.

maxPadsPerNet.description: Skip nets above this pad count (default 128)

get_schematic_component.name: get_schematic_component
get_schematic_component.description: Get full component info from a schematic: position, every field's value, and each field's label position (at x/y/angle). Returns ALL properties — both built-in fields (Reference, Value, Footprint, Datasheet) and any custom BOM/sourcing properties present on the symbol (MPN, Manufacturer, DigiKey_PN, LCSC, Voltage, Tolerance, Dielectric, etc.). Use this before edit_schematic_component / set_schematic_component_property to inspect what is currently set, or to plan a label repositioning.

get_schematic_pin_locations.name: get_schematic_pin_locations
get_schematic_pin_locations.description: Returns the exact x/y coordinates of every pin on a schematic component. Use this before add_schematic_net_label to place labels correctly on pin endpoints.

reference.description: Component reference designator (e.g. U1, R1, J2)

get_schematic_view.name: get_schematic_view
get_schematic_view.description: Return a rasterized image of the schematic (PNG by default, or SVG). Uses kicad-cli to export SVG, then converts to PNG via cairosvg. Use this for visual feedback after placing or wiring components.

get_schematic_view_region.name: get_schematic_view_region
get_schematic_view_region.description: Export a cropped region of the schematic as an image (PNG or SVG). Specify bounding box coordinates in schematic mm. Useful for zooming into a specific area to inspect wiring or layout.

x1.description: Left X coordinate of the region in mm

y1.description: Top Y coordinate of the region in mm

x2.description: Right X coordinate of the region in mm

y2.description: Bottom Y coordinate of the region in mm

get_sheet_properties.name: get_sheet_properties
get_sheet_properties.description: List hierarchical sheets in a schematic with their name, file, uuid, position, and full property map (built-ins plus custom properties set via set_sheet_property). With sheetName or sheetPath, returns just that sheet.

get_stackup.name: get_stackup
get_stackup.description: Read the stackup from the saved board file, not the board open in memory. Returns each copper, dielectric, mask, and silk entry with its thickness in millimetres. A thickness the stackup editor has locked is returned as thicknessMm plus thicknessLocked. Layer names are the names stored on the board, so a renamed layer such as 'Top Side' is returned beside the canonical F.Cu name. If an earlier save was refused, the file can be older than the session. Pass expected to compare those rows with a recipe in the same call; thicknessToleranceMm defaults to 0.001 mm and epsilonTolerance defaults to 0.01.

layer.description: Canonical name such as F.Cu, or the name stored on the board

expected.description: Rows to compare. Each row needs index or layer. Omit to only read the stackup

thicknessToleranceMm.description: Allowed thickness difference in millimetres. Default 0.001

get_symbol_info.name: get_symbol_info
get_symbol_info.description: Get detailed information about a specific symbol (global or project-scope when projectPath is supplied or a project has been opened).

projectPath.description: Optional: project directory or .kicad_pro/.kicad_pcb/.kicad_sch path so project-scope libraries are searched.

get_wire_connections.name: get_wire_connections
get_wire_connections.description: Returns the net name and all wires and component pins connected at a given point. Accepts either a component reference + pin number (e.g. reference='U1', pin='3') or a schematic coordinate (x, y in mm). Returns net=null for unnamed (unlabelled) nets. The query point must be at a wire endpoint or junction — midpoints are not matched. Use get_schematic_pin_locations or list_schematic_wires to obtain exact endpoint coordinates.

reference.description: Component reference (e.g. U1, R1). Pair with pin.

pin.description: Pin number or name (e.g. '3', 'SDA'). Pair with reference.

x.description: X coordinate of a wire endpoint in mm. Pair with y.

y.description: Y coordinate of a wire endpoint in mm. Pair with x.

group_components.name: group_components
group_components.description: Put PCB footprints into a named KiCad group (what Ctrl+G does in the PCB editor), so they select, move and rotate together; saved in the .kicad_pcb. An existing group with the same name is extended. A footprint can be in only one group, so one already in another group is moved (reported in movedFromOtherGroup). Fails without changing anything if a reference is not on the board. Returns {success, group: {name, created, members}, added}.

references.description: Reference designators of the footprints to group, e.g. ['U1', 'C1', 'C2']

groupName.description: Group name; an existing group with this name is extended

hierarchical_place.name: hierarchical_place
hierarchical_place.description: Cluster a board's footprints by their schematic-sheet hierarchy (the HierPlace algorithm). After sync_schematic_to_board piles every footprint at the origin, this packs each functional block together as a starting point for manual placement. File-based: reads and rewrites the .kicad_pcb on disk, so save any in-memory board edits first. Locked footprints are left in place.

boardPath.description: Absolute path to the .kicad_pcb file to re-place

import_3d_model.name: import_3d_model
import_3d_model.description: Copy a 3D model file (.step/.stp/.wrl/.x3d/.iges) into the project's *.3dshapes library folder and return a portable ${KIPRJMOD}/... path. Feed the returned 'modelPath' straight into add_footprint_3d_model or add_component_3d_model.

modelPath.description: Path to the source 3D model file to import

projectPath.description: Path to the .kicad_pro file or the project directory (used to locate the .3dshapes folder and compute ${KIPRJMOD})

libraryDir.description: Target *.3dshapes directory (absolute, or relative to the project). Default: <project>/<project>.3dshapes

newName.description: Rename the copied file (source extension kept if omitted)

overwrite.description: Overwrite an existing destination file (default false)

import_eagle_project.name: import_eagle_project
import_eagle_project.description: Import an Eagle project (.brd + .sch) and convert it to a KiCad project. Converts the PCB layout via kicad-cli and translates the schematic from Eagle XML to KiCad S-expression format.

board_file.description: Absolute path to the Eagle .brd board file

schematic_file.description: Absolute path to the Eagle .sch schematic file (auto-detected from .brd path if omitted)

output_dir.description: Output directory for the KiCad project (defaults to a subdirectory next to the .brd file)

project_name.description: KiCad project name (defaults to the .brd filename without extension)

import_pcb.name: import_pcb
import_pcb.description: Import a vendor PCB file (PADS, Altium, Eagle, CADSTAR, Fabmaster, P-CAD, SolidWorks PCB, or a binary Cadence Allegro .brd) and convert it to a KiCad .kicad_pcb file via kicad-cli's native pcb importer. Binary Cadence Allegro .brd files must use format 'auto' (kicad-cli auto-detects the Allegro binary format; there is no 'allegro' format literal). This only imports PCB/layout data — it does not import schematics.

inputFile.description: Absolute path to the vendor PCB file to import

outputFile.description: Destination .kicad_pcb path (defaults beside inputFile, same basename)

format.description: Input format hint (default 'auto'). Use 'auto' for binary Cadence Allegro .brd files — there is no 'allegro' literal in this enum.

reportFormat.description: Capture a structured import report from kicad-cli (default 'none')

import_ses.name: import_ses
import_ses.description: Import a Specctra SES (session) file into the current PCB. Use after running Freerouting externally.

sesPath.description: Path to the .ses file to import

import_svg_logo.name: import_svg_logo
import_svg_logo.description: Imports an SVG file as filled graphic polygons onto a KiCAD PCB layer (default F.SilkS / front silkscreen). Curves are linearised automatically. Ideal for placing a company or project logo on the board.

svgPath.description: Path to the SVG logo file

x.description: X position of the logo top-left corner in mm

y.description: Y position of the logo top-left corner in mm

width.description: Target width of the logo in mm (height is scaled to preserve aspect ratio)

layer.description: PCB layer name, e.g. F.SilkS or B.SilkS (default: F.SilkS)

strokeWidth.description: Outline stroke width in mm (0 = no outline, default 0)

filled.description: Fill polygons with solid colour (default true)

import_symbol.name: import_symbol
import_symbol.description: Copy a symbol from one .kicad_sym library into another, with optional rename and overwrite. The target library is created if missing. A derived symbol (one using (extends ...)) needs its parent imported into the target first.

targetLibraryPath.description: Path to the target .kicad_sym (created if missing)

overwrite.description: Overwrite if the symbol already exists in the target

install_gui_driver.name: install_gui_driver
install_gui_driver.description: Deploy the in-KiCad GUI-driver helper plugin into the user's KiCad plugin tree (opt-in). The connect path no longer installs it as a side effect. After install, set KICAD_GUI_DRIVER_ENABLE=1 in KiCad's environment and restart (or Refresh Plugins) to open the token-gated control channel.

is_dirty.name: is_dirty
is_dirty.description: Return whether the MCP knows the loaded board has unsaved memory changes or external disk changes.

jlc_bom_report.name: jlc_bom_report
jlc_bom_report.description:
JLCPCB assembly cost/stock review of a BOM (MCP_ISSUES S5). Groups parts by LCSC number and, per line, reports basic / preferred / extended, stock vs qtyPerBoard x boards, unit price at that quantity, the extended-part loading fee, and fee-free (basic/preferred) alternatives in the same package whose parameters are compatible (value equal; tolerance, voltage, power, current, dielectric equal or better). ICs and other parts without a parametric class get no automatic suggestion. Reads the local JLC catalog read-only (run download_jlcpcb_database first).
Source: schematicPath (DNP / not-in-BOM parts skipped, 'exclude' refs left out as hand-soldered) or bom rows [{lcsc, refs?, qty?, value?, footprint?}].
Returns {totals:{lines, parts, boards, basicLines, preferredLines, extendedLines, loadingFee ($), partsCost ($), stockShort, notFound, potentialFeeSaving}, lines:[{lcsc, refs, qtyTotal, libraryType, fee, stock, stockOk, unitPrice, status, alternatives:[{lcsc, libraryType, mfr, stock, unitPrice, attributes}]}], missingLcsc}. detail=summary (default) lists only lines needing attention.

bom.description: BOM rows instead of a schematic

extendedFee.description: Loading fee per unique extended part in USD (default 3)

alternatives.description: Max suggested alternatives per line, 0 to skip (default 3)

dbPath.description: Catalog file to use instead of the default

jlc_find_alternative.name: jlc_find_alternative
jlc_find_alternative.description:
Parametric JLCPCB part search (MCP_ISSUES S5). With lcsc: finds drop-in replacements for that part (same subcategory and package, compatible parameters). With constraints only: searches a subcategory/package by value, tolerance, voltage, stock and library type. Fee-free parts rank first, then stock, then price. Read-only.
Returns {reference?, filters:{subcategory, package, library, parametricClass}, count, alternatives:[{lcsc, libraryType, mfr, package, stock, unitPrice, attributes, notes?}]}. notes say when no parametric class exists (check the datasheet).

package.description: JLC package name, exact ('0603', 'SOT-23-5') or a glob ('SOT-23*')

subcategory.description: JLC subcategory, e.g. 'Chip Resistor - Surface Mount' (default: the lcsc part's)

noFeeOnly.description: Only Basic or Preferred parts (no loading fee)

attributes.description: Extra catalog attributes that must match, e.g. {'Temperature Coefficient':'X7R'}

constraints.description: Parametric filters; any given value/tolerance/voltage replaces the reference's

limit.description: Max results (default 10, max 100)

quantity.description: Quantity for price break and stock (default 1)

dbPath.description: Catalog file to use instead of the default

job_apply.name: job_apply
job_apply.description: Write a finished job's result into the board (for autoroute: replace the .kicad_pcb with the routed and evaluated copy, then reload it). Runs on the main command thread, so it never races another edit. Refuses when the board changed in memory or on disk since the job started, or when the job's importMode=if_better check rejected the result (pass importAnyway:true to override that check only). Returns {success, boardPath, kicad:{before, after}, decision}.

jobId.description: Job id of a succeeded job

importAnyway.description: Apply even though the if_better evaluation rejected the result

job_cancel.name: job_cancel
job_cancel.description: Cancel a running background job (kills its child processes). Cancelling never changes the board: job results are only written by job_apply. Returns {state}.

job_list.name: job_list
job_list.description: List background jobs known to this server session (newest last), without results or logs. Returns {count, jobs:[{jobId, kind, state, progress, message, elapsedSeconds, stalled, ...}]}. Jobs are kept in memory; a server restart forgets them.

kind.description: Only jobs of this kind, e.g. autoroute

states.description: Only jobs in these states (queued, running, succeeded, failed, cancelled)

job_status.name: job_status
job_status.description: State of a background job started by a long tool (e.g. autoroute with async:true). Returns {jobId, kind, state: queued|running|succeeded|failed|cancelled, progress 0..1, message, elapsedSeconds, secondsSinceProgress, stalled (no progress for the job's stallTimeout), logTail:[last lines], result (when finished), applyStep:{required, applied}}. Never changes the board.

jobId.description: Job id returned by the tool that started it

logLines.description: Log lines to include (default 20, 0 for none)

includeResult.description: Include the finished job's result (default true)

kicad_gui_click.name: kicad_gui_click
kicad_gui_click.description: Activate a menu item or AUI toolbar tool by name (as shown by kicad_gui_tree). Executes immediately — no gating.

name.description: Menu label or toolbar tooltip to activate.

id.description: Explicit wx item id (skips name resolution).

kind.description: Item kind when passing an explicit id (default menu).

frame.description: Optional frame name/title filter (e.g. 'PcbFrame', 'Schematic'). Default: main frame.

kicad_gui_click_atspi.name: kicad_gui_click_atspi
kicad_gui_click_atspi.description: Backend B: activate the first accessible node matching `name` (and optional role) via do_action.

role.description: Optional role substring filter (e.g. 'push button', 'menu item').

kicad_gui_screenshot.name: kicad_gui_screenshot
kicad_gui_screenshot.description: Capture the driven frame's screen rectangle to a PNG and return its path.

path.description: Absolute path of the .png file to write, in a directory that already exists (a temp file if omitted).

frame.description: Optional frame name/title filter (e.g. 'PcbFrame', 'Schematic'). Default: main frame.

kicad_gui_tree.name: kicad_gui_tree
kicad_gui_tree.description: Enumerate the live KiCad GUI via the in-process helper: menus/submenus (name + wx id) and AUI toolbars (id + tooltip). Destructive names carry a '⚠ ' prefix.

frame.description: Optional frame name/title filter (e.g. 'PcbFrame', 'Schematic'). Default: main frame.

kicad_gui_tree_atspi.name: kicad_gui_tree_atspi
kicad_gui_tree_atspi.description: Backend B: dump KiCad's accessible widget tree (role + name) from the Linux a11y bus — zero in-KiCad code.

kicad_gui_wait_for.name: kicad_gui_wait_for
kicad_gui_wait_for.description: Poll until a shown top-level window whose title contains `title` exists (or timeout).

title.description: Substring of the window title to wait for.

kicad_pcb_snapshot.name: kicad_pcb_snapshot
kicad_pcb_snapshot.description: GUI playbook: trigger Zoom to Fit, wait for the repaint, screenshot the frame.

path.description: Absolute path of the .png file to write, in a directory that already exists (a temp file if omitted).

frame.description: Optional frame name/title filter (e.g. 'PcbFrame', 'Schematic'). Default: main frame.

kicad_reload_and_open_plugin.name: kicad_reload_and_open_plugin
kicad_reload_and_open_plugin.description: GUI playbook (plugin dev/test loop): trigger Refresh Plugins, then open the named External-Plugins entry.

name.description: Plugin menu entry to open after the refresh.

frame.description: Optional frame name/title filter (e.g. 'PcbFrame', 'Schematic'). Default: main frame.

kicad_run_action_plugin.name: kicad_run_action_plugin
kicad_run_action_plugin.description: Find the Tools > External Plugins submenu entry with the given name (e.g. 'Open kiHarness') and trigger it.

frame.description: Optional frame name/title filter (e.g. 'PcbFrame', 'Schematic'). Default: main frame.

kicad_run_drc.name: kicad_run_drc
kicad_run_drc.description: GUI playbook: open the Design Rules Checker dialog, click 'Run DRC', then scrape the violations grid into structured results.

timeout.description: Seconds to wait for the dialog (default 15).

frame.description: Optional frame name/title filter (e.g. 'PcbFrame', 'Schematic'). Default: main frame.

launch_kicad_ui.name: launch_kicad_ui
launch_kicad_ui.description: Launch KiCAD UI, optionally with a project file

projectPath.description: Optional path to .kicad_pcb file to open

autoLaunch.description: Whether to launch KiCAD if not running (default: true)

length_match.name: length_match
length_match.description: Report the routed length of nets and differential pairs against a target (R5). Length = sum of the net's track/arc lengths (vias and pad internals excluded). target defaults to the longest net in the set. Report only (read-only tool): use tune_length to add serpentine meanders. Units mm. Returns {targetMm, toleranceMm, allWithinTolerance, nets:[{net,lengthMm,deltaMm,withinTolerance,addMm,segments,vias,routed}], pairs:[{positive,negative,skewMm,withinTolerance,shorter}]}.

pairTolerance.description: Allowed pair skew in mm (default: tolerance)

lint_offgrid.name: lint_offgrid
lint_offgrid.description: Report every off-grid connection-relevant coordinate in a schematic — wire/bus endpoints, symbol origins, label/junction/no_connect anchors — and optionally snap them to the nearest grid point (fix: true). KiCad's connection grid is fixed at 50 mil (1.27 mm) and junction placement uses exact matching, so a single off-grid endpoint can poison junction placement for a whole sheet. Unlike snap_to_grid (whole-file rewrite), fixes here are byte-exact text splices that preserve file formatting; (lib_symbols) content and property field positions are never touched. Offenders more than 0.5 mm off-grid are reported as NEEDS HUMAN and never auto-snapped.

fix.description: Snap offenders in place (default false: report only)

gridSize.description: Grid spacing in mm (default: 1.27 mm = 50 mil, the KiCad connection grid)

lint_schematic_cosmetic.name: lint_schematic_cosmetic
lint_schematic_cosmetic.description: Netlist-safe cosmetic cleanup of a .kicad_sch, applied as raw-text edits that never move a symbol, pin, wire, junction, or label anchor. Pass hide_pin_names gives every top-level embedded lib_symbol a (pin_names ... (hide yes)) directive — in label-driven schematics the internal pin names duplicate the net label on the same pin. Pass orient_labels sets each net/global/hierarchical label's text angle and justify from the sheet-space outward side of the pin it sits on (rotation/mirror aware), so text reads away from the symbol body; labels not on a pin are left untouched. Complements autoplace_schematic_fields (which handles Reference/Value fields).

passes.description: Passes to run, in order (default: both)

dryRun.description: Report change counts without writing (default false)

list_drc_rules.name: list_drc_rules
list_drc_rules.description: List the custom rules in the project's .kicad_dru: name, condition, layer, severity, constraints. errors lists problems that make KiCad ignore the whole file (fileRejected). Returns {success, message, druFile, exists, fileRejected, rules, errors, warnings}.

projectPath.description: .kicad_pro whose rules to read

list_floating_labels.name: list_floating_labels
list_floating_labels.description: Returns all net labels in the schematic that are not connected to any component pin. A label is 'floating' when no component pin falls on the wire-network reachable from the label's position. Floating labels indicate misplaced or off-grid labels that cause ERC errors. Does not require the KiCAD UI to be running.

list_footprint_libraries.name: list_footprint_libraries
list_footprint_libraries.description: List available .pretty footprint libraries and their contents (first 20 footprints per library). Searches KiCAD standard install paths by default.

searchPaths.description: Override default search paths. Each entry should be a directory that contains .pretty subdirs.

list_graphics.name: list_graphics
list_graphics.description: List PCB graphic/drawing items such as gr_line, gr_arc, gr_rect, gr_text and dimensions.

layer.description: Optional layer filter, e.g. Edge.Cuts or F.SilkS

list_libraries.name: list_libraries
list_libraries.description: List all available KiCAD footprint libraries

search_paths.description: Optional additional search paths for libraries

list_library_footprints.name: list_library_footprints
list_library_footprints.description: List all footprints in a specific KiCAD library

library_name.description: Name of the library to list footprints from

filter.description: Optional filter pattern for footprint names

limit.description: Maximum number of footprints to list

list_library_symbols.name: list_library_symbols
list_library_symbols.description: List all symbols in a specific KiCAD symbol library (global or project-scope when projectPath is supplied or a project has been opened).

projectPath.description: Optional: project directory or .kicad_pro/.kicad_pcb/.kicad_sch path to resolve project-scope libraries.

list_library_table.name: list_library_table
list_library_table.description: Read a sym-lib-table or fp-lib-table: nickname, type, URI and description of every registered library. Each URI is resolved through ${KIPRJMOD}, KiCad's built-in library directories (KICAD*_SYMBOL_DIR and friends), the path variables configured in kicad_common.json and the environment, and reported with whether the file is actually there — which is how a stale row left over from a library migration shows itself. A (type "Table") row is flagged as an indirection, with a count of the libraries it stands for.

tableType.description: Which table to edit: 'symbol' (sym-lib-table, default) or 'footprint'

projectPath.description: Path to the .kicad_pro or its directory, for scope='project'

tablePath.description: Path to the table file itself, bypassing scope/projectPath resolution

list_schematic_components.name: list_schematic_components
list_schematic_components.description: List all components in a schematic with their references, values, positions, and pins. Essential for inspecting what's on the schematic before making edits.

list_schematic_labels.name: list_schematic_labels
list_schematic_labels.description: List all net labels, global labels, and power flags in the schematic. Optionally filter by label name (netName) and/or label type (labelType).

netName.description: Filter to labels whose name exactly matches this string (case-sensitive). Omit to return all labels.

labelType.description: Filter by label type. 'net' = local label, 'global' = global label, 'power' = power symbol. Omit to return all types.

list_schematic_nets.name: list_schematic_nets
list_schematic_nets.description: List all nets in the schematic with their connections.

list_schematic_texts.name: list_schematic_texts
list_schematic_texts.description: List all free-form text annotations (notes, headings, documentation strings) in the schematic. Returns position, angle, font size, bold/italic flags, and justification for each text element. Optionally filter by a substring match on the text content.

text.description: Case-insensitive substring filter — only return texts containing this string

list_schematic_wires.name: list_schematic_wires
list_schematic_wires.description: List all wires in the schematic with start/end coordinates.

list_snapshots.name: list_snapshots
list_snapshots.description:
List project snapshots in <project>/snapshots, newest first (MCP_ISSUES I1): manual ones from snapshot_project (kind 'legacy'), automatic ones taken before mutating tools when KICAD_MCP_AUTO_SNAPSHOT=1 (kind 'auto'; last KICAD_MCP_AUTO_SNAPSHOT_KEEP kept, default 20) and 'safety' ones taken by restore_snapshot. Read-only.
Returns {count, snapshots:[{id, label, kind, tool, created, files}], autoSnapshot:{enabled, keep}}.

projectPath.description: Project directory or any project file (default: the loaded board's)

limit.description: Max entries (default 20)

list_symbol_libraries.name: list_symbol_libraries
list_symbol_libraries.description: List all available KiCAD symbol libraries from global sym-lib-table, plus the project's sym-lib-table when projectPath (or any related file) is supplied or a project has been opened.

projectPath.description: Optional: project directory or .kicad_pro/.kicad_pcb/.kicad_sch path. Including this exposes project-scope sym-lib-table libraries.

list_symbol_pins.name: list_symbol_pins
list_symbol_pins.description: Return pin names, numbers, and types for a symbol directly from the library — no schematic required. Use this before add_schematic_component to discover pins for connect_to_net calls. Each pin has 'number' (e.g. '1', 'A5') and 'name' (e.g. 'FB', 'GND') — connect_to_net accepts either. Pass schematicPath to resolve project-local symbols. Returns close-match suggestions if the symbol name is slightly wrong.

schematicPath.description: Path to .kicad_sch — enables project-local sym-lib-table lookup

list_symbols_in_library.name: list_symbols_in_library
list_symbols_in_library.description: List all symbol names in a .kicad_sym library file.

modify_trace.name: modify_trace
modify_trace.description: Modify an existing trace (change width, layer, or net).

traceUuid.description: UUID of the trace to modify

layer.description: New layer name

move_component.name: move_component
move_component.description: Move a PCB component to a new position. Optionally update rotation or flip to a different copper layer.

position.description: New position coordinates and unit

layer.description: Optional target layer (e.g., 'F.Cu', 'B.Cu') - flips component if needed

move_components.name: move_components
move_components.description: Move/rotate/flip several footprints with collision feedback (MCP_ISSUES E2). For each part returns position, overlaps and newOverlaps (courtyard polygons, same side), outsideBoard, keepouts (rule areas forbidding footprints/pads), and airwireMm {before, after} (sum of distances from its pads to the nearest same-net pad). dryRun measures at the proposed spots and restores. Returns {success, message, parts: [...], collisionsAdded, drc?}.

dx.description: Relative move in X (mm), instead of x/y

rejectOnCollision.description: Undo everything if any part gains an overlap, leaves the board, or enters a keepout

skipPlaneNets.description: Leave nets that have a zone out of airwire lengths (default true)

dryRun.description: Validate and report the would-be change without touching the board

drcDelta.description: Save now and run DRC (project rules) to report violations this edit added/resolved (slower: one DRC, two when the last recorded run is stale)

refillZones.description: Refill zones in the drcDelta DRC run (default true)

projectPath.description: .kicad_pro whose rules the drcDelta DRC uses (default: the board's project)

move_footprint_text.name: move_footprint_text
move_footprint_text.description: Move or update a footprint Reference/Value/user text field without moving the footprint.

field.description: Text field to move, e.g. reference or value

layer.description: Optional destination layer

move_schematic_component.name: move_schematic_component
move_schematic_component.description: Move a placed symbol to a new position in the schematic. By default (preserveWires=true) wire endpoints touching the component's pins are stretched to follow the new position, no-connect flags and net labels on those pins come along, and bends left diagonal by the stretch are squared up again. For a multi-unit part pass unit to say which placement to move.

position.description: New position in schematic mm coordinates

preserveWires.description: Stretch connected wire endpoints to follow the move, carrying the attached net labels, no-connect flags and wire bends along so the routing stays orthogonal (default true)

straightenWires.description: Square up wire bends that the stretch turned diagonal, by carrying the neighbouring corner along with the pin (default true). Set false to leave stretched segments exactly as the drag left them.

unit.description: Unit of a multi-unit part (1=A, 2=B, …). Every unit of a part shares one reference, so without this the tool acts on whichever placement comes first in the file. Omit for single-unit parts.

move_schematic_net_label.name: move_schematic_net_label
move_schematic_net_label.description: Move a net label (local, global, or hierarchical) to a new position in the schematic. Use currentPosition to disambiguate when multiple labels share the same name.

netName.description: Name of the net label to move

currentPosition.description: Current position to disambiguate when multiple labels share the same name

labelType.description: Restrict search to a specific label type

net_report.name: net_report
net_report.description: Per-net routing report in one call: track length per layer, via count and sizes, layers used, track width min/max, island count / fully-connected flag (from KiCad's connectivity), plane-split crossings and reference voids under the net's tracks, and named regions the net enters. Units: mm, KiCad board coordinates (absolute positions as stored in the .kicad_pcb, +y down; not relative to a grid or aux origin). Split crossings: for each track the nearest copper layers above/below that carry zones are its reference planes; a crossing is where the zone net under the track changes (e.g. GND -> +3V3 on In2.Cu); a void is a stretch of at least minVoidMm with no plane copper under the track. Returns {netCount, notFullyConnected, planeLayers, netsWithSplitCrossings, nets:[{net, pads, tracks, vias, zones, lengthMm, islands, fullyConnected, unroutedConnections, splitCrossings, referenceVoids, lengthByLayer?, layers?, zoneLayers?, widthMm?, viaSizes?, crossings?:[{at,layer,refLayer,from,to}], voids?, regions?}], warnings?}. With nets: default detail is items (crossing lists capped at 5 per net; full = all). Without nets: every net, detail summary, problems first, limit 25.

nets.description: Net names (a name without '/' may match a hierarchical net's last component). Omit for all nets.

detail.description: summary = counts only; items = counts + compact rows; full = rows + uuids and extra fields

limit.description: Maximum nets returned (default 25)

planeCrossings.description: Compute split crossings and voids (default true)

referenceLayers.description: Restrict which copper layers count as reference planes (default: every layer that has zones)

minVoidMm.description: Shortest plane-free stretch reported as a void (default 1.0 mm)

regions.description: Named regions, {"AUDIO": [[x,y],...] or {x0,y0,x1,y1}}; each net reports the regions it enters

boardPath.description: Absolute path to a .kicad_pcb to read fresh from disk. Omit to use the board loaded in memory (unsaved edits included).

open_board.name: open_board
open_board.description: Open a specific .kicad_pcb board file and refresh the MCP in-memory board state.

boardPath.description: Path to the .kicad_pcb file to open

place_component.name: place_component
place_component.description: Place a footprint component onto the PCB at the specified position. Optionally set reference, value, footprint, rotation and layer.

componentId.description: Identifier for the component to place (e.g., 'R_0603_10k')

position.description: Position coordinates and unit

layer.description: Optional layer (e.g., 'F.Cu', 'B.SilkS')

boardPath.description: Path to the .kicad_pcb file – required when using project-local footprint libraries

place_component_array.name: place_component_array
place_component_array.description: Place a rectangular grid array of identical components on the PCB with configurable row/column spacing.

place_relative.name: place_relative
place_relative.description: Place a part relative to another part or one of its pads, e.g. a decoupling cap next to an IC supply pin (MCP_ISSUES E2). Target = anchor origin (or anchorPad centre) + offset; with pad, that pad of `ref` lands on the target instead of its origin. alignToAnchor turns the offset and rotation into the anchor's frame. Same collision feedback as move_components. Returns {success, message, target, anchor, parts, drc?}.

anchorPad.description: Pad number on the anchor to measure from

offset.description: [dx, dy] mm from the anchor point (default [0, 0])

rotation.description: Rotation in degrees (absolute, or relative with alignToAnchor)

alignToAnchor.description: Offset/rotation in the anchor's rotated frame

pad.description: Pad of `ref` to put on the target

rejectOnCollision.description: Undo everything if any part gains an overlap, leaves the board, or enters a keepout

skipPlaneNets.description: Leave nets that have a zone out of airwire lengths (default true)

dryRun.description: Validate and report the would-be change without touching the board

drcDelta.description: Save now and run DRC (project rules) to report violations this edit added/resolved (slower: one DRC, two when the last recorded run is stale)

refillZones.description: Refill zones in the drcDelta DRC run (default true)

projectPath.description: .kicad_pro whose rules the drcDelta DRC uses (default: the board's project)

project_status.name: project_status
project_status.description: About 10 lines to re-orient after a context reset: sheet and part counts, board footprint and unrouted counts, schematic<->board parity (refs missing on either side), the last DRC/ERC counts (cached from run_drc/run_erc, never re-run here), unsaved board state and the last snapshot. Read-only and cheap; call it instead of re-reading files.

projectPath.description: A .kicad_pro, .kicad_sch, .kicad_pcb or project directory (default: the loaded board's project)

detail.description: summary (default): the text lines only. full: also the structured fields.

query_region.name: query_region
query_region.description: List what is inside a window of the board: pads, vias, tracks, arcs, zones, rule areas and text (footprints and graphics on request), as a compact table. Units: mm, KiCad board coordinates (absolute positions as stored in the .kicad_pcb, +y down; not relative to a grid or aux origin). Returns {count, byKind, nets, columns:["kind","id","net","layer","geom","info","locked"], rows, truncated?, omitted?}. geom is [x,y] for pads/vias/text, [x1,y1,x2,y2] for tracks, [x1,y1,xm,ym,x2,y2] for arcs, [x,y,rot] for footprints and the outline bbox for zones. id is REF.PAD for pads and the first 8 uuid characters for tracks/vias (connected_items accepts that prefix). info holds size/width ("rect 0.28x0.665", "w0.2", "0.6/0.3" via dia/drill), or for zones whether fill exists inside the window. Items are included when their copper touches the window. detail "summary" returns counts by kind, layer and net only. Default: detail "items", limit 60.

layers.description: Only items on these layers, e.g. ["F.Cu","In1.Cu"] (board or legacy names accepted)

kinds.description: Item kinds to include (default: pad, via, track, arc, zone, rule_area, text)

nets.description: Only items on these nets. A name without '/' also matches the last path component (SDA matches /MCU/SDA). Text and graphics are dropped when filtering by net.

detail.description: summary = counts only; items = counts + compact rows; full = rows + uuids and extra fields

limit.description: Maximum rows returned

boardPath.description: Absolute path to a .kicad_pcb to read fresh from disk. Omit to use the board loaded in memory (unsaved edits included).

query_traces.name: query_traces
query_traces.description: Query traces on the board with optional filters by net, layer, or bounding box.

layer.description: Filter by layer name

query_zones.name: query_zones
query_zones.description: Query copper zones (filled pours) on the board with optional filters by net, layer, or bounding box. Returns zone net, layers, priority, fill state, and bounding box. Useful for auditing power planes and GND pours that query_traces does not include.

layer.description: Filter by layer name (matches zones that include this layer)

boundingBox.description: Filter to zones whose bounding box overlaps this region

refill_zones.description: Refill all copper zones on the board. WARNING: SWIG path has known segfault risk (see KNOWN_ISSUES.md). Prefer using IPC backend (KiCAD open) or triggering zone fill via KiCAD UI instead.

register_footprint_library.name: register_footprint_library
register_footprint_library.description: Register a .pretty footprint library in KiCAD's fp-lib-table so KiCAD can find the footprints. Run this after create_footprint when KiCAD shows 'library not found in footprint library table'.

libraryPath.description: Full path to the .pretty directory to register

libraryName.description: Nickname for the library in KiCAD (default: directory name without .pretty)

scope.description: project = writes fp-lib-table next to the .kicad_pro file (default); global = writes to the user's global KiCAD config

projectPath.description: Path to the .kicad_pro file or its directory (required for scope=project when the library is not in the project folder)

register_symbol_library.name: register_symbol_library
register_symbol_library.description: Register a .kicad_sym library in KiCAD's sym-lib-table so symbols can be used in schematics. Run this after create_symbol when KiCAD shows 'library not found'.

scope.description: project = writes sym-lib-table next to .kicad_pro; global = user config

projectPath.description: Path to .kicad_pro or its directory (for scope=project)

relabel_net.name: relabel_net
relabel_net.description:
Rename one net across the sheet hierarchy. oldName is a label text ("+5V") or a KiCad
net path ("/Power/+5V"; "/+5V" for the root sheet). Global labels named oldName are
renamed on every sheet. Local labels are per sheet, so they (and hierarchical labels) are
renamed only on the sheet the net path names - or, for a plain name, on schematicPath -
and wherever that same net continues: through a sheet pin into the child's hierarchical
label, from a hierarchical label up to the parent sheet pin and the parent's label, or by
being wired to a renamed global label. Same-named local labels on other sheets are
different nets and are left alone (listed in untouchedLocalLabels with their net paths).
Parent sheet pins bound to a renamed hierarchical label are renamed with it so the sheet
interface stays connected. Power symbols are left alone unless includePowerSymbols=true
(their Value is the net name). sheetOnly=true limits label renames to schematicPath
itself. Edits are textual; nothing else in the files changes. dryRun=true reports what
would change without writing.

Returns {success, dryRun, message, renamed, changes:[{file, label?, global_label?,
hierarchical_label?, sheet_pin?, power_symbol?}], rootSchematic, sheetsScanned,
untouchedLocalLabels?:[{file, labels, netPath}]}.

schematicPath.description: A .kicad_sch of the project: the hierarchy from its root is scanned, and for a plain oldName this is the sheet whose local labels are renamed

oldName.description: Current label text, or net path '/Sheet/NAME' naming the sheet of a local net

sheetOnly.description: Only rename labels on schematicPath itself (default false)

includePowerSymbols.description: Also change the Value of power symbols named oldName (default false)

dryRun.description: Report the changes without writing (default false)

reload_board.name: reload_board
reload_board.description: Reload the current or specified .kicad_pcb from disk, discarding stale in-memory board state.

boardPath.description: Optional .kicad_pcb path; defaults to current board

remove_copper.name: remove_copper
remove_copper.description: Remove tracks/arcs/vias matching a filter (MCP_ISSUES E1). Needs at least one of nets, region or endpointNear. Locked copper is kept unless filter.locked is 'locked' or 'any' (the result says how many were kept). Returns {success, message, removed: {count, byKind, byNet}, items (first `limit`), skippedLocked?, drc?}.

regionMode.description: inside (default): wholly inside the region; touch: any part

endpointNear.description: Items with an end (or via centre) within radius mm (default 0.05)

layer.description: Only this copper layer (vias spanning it)

limit.description: Max removed items listed (default 20)

dryRun.description: Validate and report the would-be change without touching the board

drcDelta.description: Save now and run DRC (project rules) to report violations this edit added/resolved (slower: one DRC, two when the last recorded run is stale)

refillZones.description: Refill zones in the drcDelta DRC run (default true)

projectPath.description: .kicad_pro whose rules the drcDelta DRC uses (default: the board's project)

remove_drc_rule.name: remove_drc_rule
remove_drc_rule.description: Remove custom rule(s) by name from the project's .kicad_dru (atomic write; comments directly above a rule go with it). Returns {success, message, removed, remaining, dryRun}.

dryRun.description: Report without writing

projectPath.description: .kicad_pro whose rules to edit

remove_hierarchical_sheet.name: remove_hierarchical_sheet
remove_hierarchical_sheet.description: Remove a hierarchical-sheet reference from a parent schematic (the reverse of add_hierarchical_sheet). Identify the sheet by sheetName (matches the sheet's name property) or by subsheetPath (matched by basename against the sheet's file property). Deletes the (sheet ...) block and any matching (sheet_instances) page entry. Does NOT delete the sub-sheet .kicad_sch file on disk.

sheetName.description: Sheet display name to remove (matches the Sheetname/Sheet name property)

subsheetPath.description: Sub-sheet file to remove (matched by basename against the Sheetfile property)

remove_library_table_entry.name: remove_library_table_entry
remove_library_table_entry.description: Remove one or more entries from a sym-lib-table or fp-lib-table by nickname — the counterpart to register_symbol_library / register_footprint_library. The table is re-parsed before it is written, so an edit that would leave it unbalanced is refused rather than saved; the write is atomic and the previous contents are kept in a sibling .mcp-backups/ directory. Use dryRun first when the target is scope='global', which every project on the machine loads. Removing a (type "Table") row unregisters every library in the table it points at, and the result says so.

tableType.description: Which table to edit: 'symbol' (sym-lib-table, default) or 'footprint'

projectPath.description: Path to the .kicad_pro or its directory, for scope='project'

tablePath.description: Path to the table file itself, bypassing scope/projectPath resolution

dryRun.description: Report what the edit would do without writing the table

libraryNames.description: Several nicknames to remove in one pass

remove_schematic_component_property.name: remove_schematic_component_property
remove_schematic_component_property.description:
Remove a single custom property from a placed schematic symbol.

Built-in fields (Reference, Value, Footprint, Datasheet) cannot be removed —
KiCad requires them on every symbol. To clear a built-in field, use
edit_schematic_component and set its value to an empty string.

reference.description: Reference designator of the component (e.g. R1, U3)

rename_symbol.name: rename_symbol
rename_symbol.description: Rename a symbol in a .kicad_sym library, including its sub-symbol shards (name_0_1, ...) and any (extends ...) references from derived symbols in the same library. Note: schematics that already place the old lib_id are NOT updated — use replace_instance_lib_ids for that.

repair_flat_symbols.name: repair_flat_symbols
repair_flat_symbols.description:
Repair "flat" vendor symbols so schematic tools can parse the file.

SnapEDA/SamacSys .kicad_sym captures often put pins and graphics directly
under the top-level (symbol "NAME" ...) with no _1_1 sub-unit. KiCad and
kicad-cli tolerate this, but the kicad-skip parser used by the schematic
edit/inspect tools (list_schematic_components, batch_connect, ...) crashes
on it — for any sheet that uses, or embeds a snapshot of, such a symbol.

This tool wraps the drawable/pin children in a proper (symbol "NAME_1_1")
sub-unit via pure text insertion (formatting preserved, render-neutral).
Works on standalone .kicad_sym libraries and on the embedded (lib_symbols)
block of a .kicad_sch. Idempotent; already-wrapped and extends-derived
symbols are skipped. Dry-run by default — files are edited in place, so
keep them under version control before repairing.

dryRun.description: Report flat symbols without writing (default true)

replace_board_outline.name: replace_board_outline
replace_board_outline.description: Replace the current Edge.Cuts board outline with a rectangle, rounded rectangle, circle or polygon.

replace_component.name: replace_component
replace_component.description: Swap a placed PCB footprint for another library footprint, keeping its reference, value, position, rotation, board side, schematic link, custom fields and pad nets (matched by pad number). Returns {success, component: {reference, value, footprint, previousFootprint, position: {x, y, unit: 'mm'}, rotation (deg), side}, padNetsKept, droppedPadNets?} - droppedPadNets lists old pad numbers with nets that the new footprint does not have.

reference.description: Reference designator of the component to replace

newComponentId.description: Alternative to newFootprint: 'Library:Footprint' or a bare footprint name searched in every library

replace_instance_lib_ids.name: replace_instance_lib_ids
replace_instance_lib_ids.description: Replace lib_id references in schematic symbol instances per an explicit old-to-new mapping — the mechanical layer of a library migration (e.g. eagle_import symbols to curated library symbols). Mirror-variant suffixes (__m0/__m90/__m180/__m270) get automatic angle correction; each needs its own mapping entry. Only instances are rewritten; lib_symbols is preserved (use update_symbol_from_library to refresh definitions afterwards).

mapping.description: Map of old full lib_id to new full lib_id, e.g. {"eagle_import:C_100n": "Device:C"}. Values are used verbatim.

sourceLibrary.description: Library prefix whose instances are candidates

replace_schematic_component.name: replace_schematic_component
replace_schematic_component.description: Replace a placed component's symbol with a different one (e.g. Device:R -> Device:R_Potentiometer), preserving its position, rotation, and field values (Value/Footprint/custom). Optionally override rotation with newRotation. Returns the new pin positions.

reference.description: Reference of the component to replace (e.g., D1)

newRotation.description: Override rotation in degrees (default: keep existing)

restore_snapshot.name: restore_snapshot
restore_snapshot.description:
Restore the design files (.kicad_pcb/.kicad_sch/.kicad_pro/...) held by a snapshot (MCP_ISSUES I1). Takes a 'safety' snapshot of the files it will overwrite first (restore that to undo), writes each file atomically, and reloads the in-memory board when the loaded board is restored. Files not in the snapshot are kept. Refuses when the loaded board has unsaved changes unless force=true.
Returns {files:[{path, action: overwrite|create|unchanged}], changedFiles, safetySnapshot, keptFilesNotInSnapshot, boardReloaded?}.

snapshot.description: Snapshot id, label, unique id fragment, or 'latest'

projectPath.description: Project directory or any project file (default: the loaded board's)

dryRun.description: Only report what would be restored

files.description: Restore only these files (paths relative to the project, or file names)

rotate_component.description: Rotate a PCB component to an absolute angle in degrees.

rotate_schematic_component.description: Rotate a placed symbol in the schematic. For a multi-unit part pass unit to say which placement to rotate.

angle.description: Absolute rotation in degrees (0, 90, 180, 270). This is the symbol's final orientation, not a relative increment — passing 90 sets the symbol to 90° regardless of its current angle (unlike KiCad's UI 'R' key).

straightenWires.description: Square up wire bends that the rotation turned diagonal (default true).

unit.description: Unit of a multi-unit part (1=A, 2=B, …). Every unit of a part shares one reference, so without this the tool acts on whichever placement comes first in the file. Omit for single-unit parts.

route_arc_trace.name: route_arc_trace
route_arc_trace.description: Route a copper arc trace defined by start/mid/end points. Uses true PCB arc primitives when available.

layer.description: PCB layer

route_bus.name: route_bus
route_bus.description: Route several connections as a bus (e.g. an I2S/MCLK bundle). mode 'parallel' (default) routes a true parallel bundle: one guide corridor wide enough for every member is found with the A* router (on `layer`; layer changes only with allowVias and pitch >= via + clearance), each member's trunk is the guide offset by its lane x pitch with miter joins (octilinear, spacing = pitch measured perpendicular; outer traces are longer on bends), members are ordered across the bundle by their start pads (or `order`), and short A* fan-in/fan-out legs join the pads to the trunk ends. Everything is re-checked with exact clearance before an all-or-nothing write. If no corridor/legs/clearance work it falls back to mode 'sequential' and says why (modeUsed, fallbackReason). mode 'sequential' routes the connections one after another, later ones treating earlier ones as obstacles with mutual clearance pitch - width (no parallel geometry). Typical time: 1-5 s for 3-4 nets over 40 mm on a dense 4-layer board. Units mm. Returns {modeUsed, fallbackReason?, results:[per member: net, from, to, offsetMm, lengthMm, trunkLengthMm, legLengthsMm, segments, vias], lengths, lengthSpreadMm, segments, vias, order, pitch, layer, guide, parallelism:[{nets, trunkAtPitch, routeAtPitch}], notes, written}.

pad.description: Pad number/name on that footprint, e.g. 44

layer.description: Copper layer for an {x,y} endpoint, e.g. F.Cu

connections.description: Bus members (sequential mode: routing order). Omit from/to to route each net's closest missing connection

pitch.description: Centre-to-centre spacing between bus members in mm (parallel default: width + clearance rounded up to 0.05; raised to that minimum if smaller)

order.description: Parallel: nets from left to right looking from the 'from' end along the bundle (default: by start pad position)

layer.description: Parallel: layer of the bundle trunk (default: preferLayer or the first allowed layer)

allowVias.description: Parallel: let the trunk change layers (needs pitch >= via size + clearance) and the legs use vias (default false)

breakoutRadius.description: Parallel: fixed distance in mm from each end's pad centroid where the trunk may start/end (default: adaptive)

legRoom.description: Parallel: extra room in mm kept between the pads and the trunk ends for the fan-in legs (default 0.8, + via size with allowVias)

timeBudget.description: Parallel: seconds to spend before falling back to sequential (default 60)

width.description: Track width in mm (default: the net class width)

via.description: Via size/drill in mm (default: the net's net-class via)

clearance.description: Clearance to other-net copper in mm (default: the larger of the two nets' net-class clearances; .kicad_dru custom rules are not applied, run DRC after)

avoidRegions.description: Regions the route must not enter (tracks and vias)

searchMargin.description: Search window margin around the two ends in mm before the whole board (default 8)

locked.description: Lock the written tracks/vias so autorouters keep them (default false)

dryRun.description: Plan and check only; write nothing

route_connection.name: route_connection
route_connection.description: Route one connection of a net with a grid A* router (R3): 45-degree moves on the allowed copper layers, layer changes through vias, obstacles = other-net pads/tracks/vias inflated by clearance + half width, rule areas that forbid tracks/vias, the board edge, and avoidRegions. Same-net copper is free, so the route may start/end anywhere on the copper already connected to each end. from/to are {ref,pad} or {x,y,layer}; omit both to route the closest connection KiCad reports as missing on the net. The path is re-checked with exact geometry before writing. Typical time: well under a second for an open 40 mm route, a few seconds when a fine-pitch pin needs the refined grid. Units mm. Returns {net, from, to, lengthMm, segments, vias, layersUsed, path:[{x,y,layer}], written, stats} or alreadyConnected:true. Nothing is written with dryRun; the board is unchanged on failure.

route_differential_pair.name: route_differential_pair
route_differential_pair.description: Route a differential pair as two parallel straight segments. startPos and endPos are the pair's centreline; looking from start to end on the board (y down), the positive trace runs on the right and the negative on the left, each offset by (gap + width) / 2. Pass targetImpedance (differential ohms) to size width or gap from the layer's stackup. The result always reports impedance: the estimated Zdiff, Zodd and Zeven for the width and gap actually used (closed-form, about +/-5% of a field solver; solder mask not modelled).

layer.description: PCB layer

width.description: Trace width in mm. Optional with targetImpedance (solved from the stackup); otherwise defaults to the board's current track width

gap.description: Edge-to-edge gap between the two traces in mm. Defaults to the net class diff-pair gap with targetImpedance, else 0.2

targetImpedance.description: Differential impedance target in ohms, e.g. 90 for USB or 100 for Ethernet/LVDS. When width and gap are not both given, the missing one is solved from the layer's stackup: a given width is kept and the gap solved, otherwise the gap is kept and the width solved

route_pad_to_pad.name: route_pad_to_pad
route_pad_to_pad.description: PREFERRED tool for pad-to-pad routing. Looks up pad positions automatically, detects the net from the pad, and — critically — if the two pads are on different copper layers (e.g. J1 on F.Cu and J2 on B.Cu) automatically inserts a via at the midpoint so the connection is complete. Always use this instead of route_trace when routing between named component pads.

fromPad.description: Pad number on the source component (e.g. '6' or 6)

toPad.description: Pad number on the target component (e.g. '15' or 15)

layer.description: PCB layer (default: F.Cu)

width.description: Trace width in mm (default: board default)

net.description: Net name override (default: auto-detected from pad)

route_trace.name: route_trace
route_trace.description: Route a trace segment between two XY points on a fixed layer. WARNING: Does NOT handle layer changes — if start and end are on different copper layers, use route_pad_to_pad instead, which automatically inserts a via.

layer.description: PCB layer

run_drc.name: run_drc
run_drc.description: Run the KiCAD Design Rule Check (DRC) on the saved PCB with kicad-cli, against the project's own .kicad_pro/.kicad_dru (`rules` says which were used). Includes unconnected items and, on request, schematic-parity issues. Compact by default: counts by type/severity plus the first `limit` violations with coordinates (mm), and a `delta` (new/resolved) against the previous run on this board. Use `ignore`/`nets`/`refs`/`region` to narrow, detail='full' for everything. The full list is also saved to `violationsFile`. Zones are refilled first by default, as in KiCad's DRC dialog.

reportPath.description: Optional path to save the DRC report

refillZones.description: Refill all zones before checking (default true, like the DRC dialog). Stale fills report clearance errors that a refill would clear.

schematicParity.description: Also check the board against the project's schematic (default false)

projectPath.description: .kicad_pro (or its directory) whose rules to apply. Default: the board's own project, else the only .kicad_pro next to the board.

standards.description: Append the project's standards profile result (standards.yaml/.json, see check_standards) when one exists (default true)

detail.description: summary (default): counts by type/severity + the first `limit` items with coordinates (mm). items: every matching item. full: also the legacy `violations` list with item UUIDs.

limit.description: Max items listed (default 20 for summary, all for items/full)

nets.description: Only violations naming one of these nets ('+5V' also matches '/Power/+5V')

refs.description: Only violations naming one of these references, e.g. ['U3', 'C12']

region.description: Only violations with an item inside this box (mm)

timeoutSec.description: kicad-cli timeout in seconds (default 600 for DRC, 300 for ERC; max 1800)

run_erc.name: run_erc
run_erc.description: Runs the KiCAD Electrical Rules Check (ERC) on a schematic. Compact by default: counts by type/severity, the first `limit` violations with location (mm), and a delta (new/resolved) against the previous run on this schematic. Narrow with `ignore` (type globs, e.g. 'lib_symbol_*'), `nets`, `refs` or `region`; detail='full' returns every violation as JSON. Use after wiring to verify the schematic before generating a netlist.

detail.description: summary (default): counts by type/severity + the first `limit` items with coordinates (mm). items: every matching item. full: also the legacy `violations` list with item UUIDs.

limit.description: Max items listed (default 20 for summary, all for items/full)

nets.description: Only violations naming one of these nets ('+5V' also matches '/Power/+5V')

refs.description: Only violations naming one of these references, e.g. ['U3', 'C12']

region.description: Only violations with an item inside this box (mm)

timeoutSec.description: kicad-cli timeout in seconds (default 600 for DRC, 300 for ERC; max 1800)

run_pcbnew_script.name: run_pcbnew_script
run_pcbnew_script.description:
EXECUTES ARBITRARY PYTHON CODE with the server's permissions (MCP_ISSUES I3 escape hatch). The code runs in a separate KiCad-Python subprocess against a fresh load of the board from disk (not the server's in-memory board), with a hard timeout.
Predefined: board (pcbnew.BOARD), pcbnew, args (your 'args' object), mm(v)/to_mm(v) unit helpers, footprint(ref), fpid_of(fp) ('Lib:Name', safe when GetFPID is broken), load_footprint('Lib:Name') / place_footprint(spec, ref, x_mm, y_mm, rot, layer) (list specs in preloadFootprints so they load before the board: KiCad 10 SWIG trap), zone_layers(zone), add_zone(net, layer, [[x,y],...] mm, priority, clearance, min_width, name), refill(), check(obj, cls). Set 'result = ...' or 'return ...' at top level to return JSON.
save=true saves the board atomically only if the file did not change meanwhile, then the server reloads its in-memory board from it (refused while the loaded board has unsaved changes unless discardUnsaved=true). Not available in readonly/manufacturing modes.
Returns {success, returnValue, stdout, stderr, error?, traceback?, saved, durationSec}.

timeout.description: Seconds before the script is killed (default 60, max 1800)

args.description: JSON object exposed to the script as 'args'

preloadFootprints.description: 'Lib:Name' footprints to load before the board (for load_footprint)

discardUnsaved.description: Allow save even though the loaded board has unsaved in-memory changes

The placement type controls whether the footprint is included in pick-and-place (.pos) output files. Use exclude_from_pos_files to suppress a footprint from .pos exports without changing its type.
