set_schematic_component_property.name: set_schematic_component_property
set_schematic_component_property.description:
Add or update a single custom property on a placed schematic symbol.

This is a focused convenience wrapper around edit_schematic_component for the very
common case of attaching one BOM / sourcing field at a time. The property is
created if it does not already exist on the component.

Typical custom properties:
  • MPN, Manufacturer, Manufacturer_PN — manufacturer part number metadata
  • DigiKey, DigiKey_PN, Mouser_PN, LCSC, JLCPCB_PN — distributor part numbers
  • Voltage, Tolerance, Power, Dielectric, Temperature_Coefficient — passive parameters
  • Description, Notes — free-form documentation
  • Any custom field your BOM exporter expects.

These properties are written into the .kicad_sch file as standard KiCad property
records, are exported by export_bom, and are picked up by the JLCPCB and Digi-Key
sourcing tools. Newly-created properties default to hidden — set hide=false to
display the value on the schematic canvas.

For batch updates of multiple properties at once, use edit_schematic_component
with the `properties` parameter instead.

reference.description: Reference designator of the component (e.g. R1, U3)

value.description: Property value to write (use empty string to clear)

x.description: Label X position in mm (default: component X)

y.description: Label Y position in mm (default: component Y)

hide.description: Hide the property text on the schematic canvas. Defaults to true for newly-created custom properties.

fontSize.description: Font size in mm for the label (default: 1.27)

justify.description: Text justification for the property label. KiCad alignment keywords: "left", "right", "center", "top", "bottom", or combined e.g. "left top". Omit to leave unchanged. Pass "center" to reset to the KiCad default.

set_schematic_property_position.name: set_schematic_property_position
set_schematic_property_position.description: Move a component's Reference or Value field label to an absolute (x, y) coordinate (mm), optionally rotating or hiding it. Only 'Reference' and 'Value' are supported. Use autoplace_schematic_fields to place all of them automatically.

x.description: New X position in mm (absolute schematic coordinate)

y.description: New Y position in mm (absolute schematic coordinate)

visible.description: Whether the field is visible (default true)

set_sheet_property.name: set_sheet_property
set_sheet_property.description: Add or update a custom property on a hierarchical sheet's (sheet ...) block — e.g. cell identity or generator parameters carried as sheet metadata. Identify the sheet by sheetName or sheetPath (basename match against the sheet's file property). The property is created hidden if absent, otherwise its value is updated in place; the file's formatting is preserved. The built-in 'Sheet name'/'Sheet file' properties cannot be set here — use add/remove_hierarchical_sheet to manage the sheet link.

sheetName.description: Sheet display name (matches the Sheetname/Sheet name property)

sheetPath.description: Sub-sheet file (matched by basename against the Sheetfile property)

set_stackup_layer.name: set_stackup_layer
set_stackup_layer.description: Set the thickness of one stackup row in the board file, and for a dielectric its material, relative permittivity, and loss tangent. Identify the row by index from get_stackup or by a layer name such as F.Cu or the name stored on the board. Only the fields you pass are changed. sublayer selects a dielectric piece and defaults to 0.

layer.description: Canonical name such as F.Cu, or the name stored on the board

thicknessMm.description: Thickness of this sublayer in millimetres

set_symbol_pin_type.name: set_symbol_pin_type
set_symbol_pin_type.description: Set the electrical type (and optionally the graphic style) of pins in a .kicad_sym library, filtered by symbol, pin number, pin name, or current type. Use this instead of a sed/regex pass over the library: a blind substitution also rewrites matching words inside symbol names, Descriptions and (alternate ...) pin functions, and it cannot tell which symbol it is standing on. The replacement token is checked against KiCAD's pin types first — an unknown one makes the whole library fail to load. Typical use: imported or SnapEDA symbols arrive with every pin 'unspecified' or 'bidirectional', which floods ERC with conflicts on nets that are electrically fine. Run with dryRun first to see what matches. The library is replaced atomically, keeps its existing line endings, and is copied to a sibling '.mcp-backups/' first (path returned in 'backupPath'). 'changes' lists at most 200 per-pin records, with 'changesTruncated' saying when it was cut; 'changeCount' always carries the true total.

libraryPath.description: Absolute path to the .kicad_sym library file

symbols.description: Top-level symbol names to change (not unit names like 'R_0402_1_1'). Omit to change every symbol in the library.

fromType.description: Only pins currently of this electrical type — the safe way to do a bulk fix

dryRun.description: Report what would change without writing

snap_to_grid.name: snap_to_grid
snap_to_grid.description: Snap schematic element coordinates to the nearest grid point. KiCAD uses exact integer matching for connectivity, so off-grid coordinates cause wires that look connected to fail ERC checks. Modifies the .kicad_sch file in place. Does not require the KiCAD UI to be running.

gridSize.description: Grid spacing in mm (default: 1.27 mm = 50 mil, the KiCad connection grid; do NOT use 2.54 — snapping to a 100 mil grid moves pins off their 50 mil positions and breaks connectivity)

elements.description: Element types to snap (default: ["wires", "junctions", "labels"]). "components" is opt-in — moving a component without re-routing wires creates new mismatches.

snapshot_project.name: snapshot_project
snapshot_project.description: Save a named checkpoint snapshot of the current project state (renders board to PDF and records step label). Call after completing each major step — e.g. after Step 1 (schematic_ok) and Step 2 (layout_ok). Required by the demo workflow before waiting for user confirmation.

step.description: Step number or identifier, e.g. '1' or '2'

label.description: Short label for this checkpoint, e.g. 'schematic_ok' or 'layout_ok'

prompt.description: Full prompt text to save as PROMPT_step{step}_{timestamp}.md alongside the snapshot

split_plane.name: split_plane
split_plane.description: Build a multi-net plane on one layer in one call (MCP_ISSUES E3). regions is {net: polygon} or [{net, polygon, priority?}]; earlier regions get higher priority (from basePriority, default 1) so overlaps resolve in list order. replaceExisting removes the layer's current copper zones first. Returns {success, message, layer, zones, removed, warnings, drc?}.

layer.description: Copper layer, e.g. 'In2.Cu'

additionalProperties.description: Polygon [[x, y], ...] (mm), a box {x1, y1, x2, y2}, or "board" for the board outline

replaceExisting.description: Remove the copper zones already on this layer (default false)

layerType.description: Also set the layer type (power for planes)

padConnection.description: How pads connect to the zone

dryRun.description: Validate and report the would-be change without touching the board

drcDelta.description: Save now and run DRC (project rules) to report violations this edit added/resolved (slower: one DRC, two when the last recorded run is stale)

refillZones.description: Refill zones in the drcDelta DRC run (default true)

projectPath.description: .kicad_pro whose rules the drcDelta DRC uses (default: the board's project)

stitch_ground.name: stitch_ground
stitch_ground.description: Place stitching vias for a pour net (default GND): a grid inside the net's pours, a ring along Edge.Cuts and via fences along polylines or a zone outline. Each via is checked against all other-net copper on every layer (net-class clearance + keepClear), hole-to-hole spacing, via keepouts, courtyards (courtyardPolicy) and the board edge, and is placed only where the net's filled pour covers the whole via on at least minLayers copper layers (and on every layer in requireLayers). Zones are refilled afterwards. Units mm. Returns {placed:{fence,edge,grid,total}, candidates, rejected:{reason:count}, vias:[{x,y,kind}] (first `limit`), pourLayers, clearance, minSpacing, saved}.

net.description: Pour net (default: GND / GROUND / VSS / /GND / AGND)

grid.description: Grid pitch in mm (default 2.5; 0 = no grid). Grid points must still fall in the pour.

edgePitch.description: Pitch of the edge ring along Edge.Cuts in mm (default 2.0; 0 = no ring)

edgeInset.description: Distance of the edge ring from Edge.Cuts in mm (default: copper-edge clearance + via radius + 0.25)

fencePolylines.description: Via fences: each entry is [[x,y],...] (mm), {points, closed} or {zoneName} (fence along that zone/rule-area outline)

fenceNudge.description: If a fence spot is blocked, also try this far either side of the line, mm (default 0.4)

keepClear.description: Extra clearance to other-net copper on top of the net-class clearance, mm (default 0.1)

minSpacing.description: Minimum centre distance to other vias of the net, mm (default max(via+clearance, drill+hole-to-hole))

minLayers.description: Pour of the net must cover the via on at least this many copper layers (default 2)

requireLayers.description: Layers where the pour must be present at every via, e.g. ["F.Cu","B.Cu"]

courtyardPolicy.description: Courtyards: avoid for all vias, allow everywhere, or fence_allowed (default: grid/edge avoid, fences may enter)

region.description: Only place vias inside this rectangle (mm)

limit.description: Max vias listed in the reply (default 100)

dryRun.description: Report what would be placed without changing the board

suggest_jlcpcb_alternatives.name: suggest_jlcpcb_alternatives
suggest_jlcpcb_alternatives.description:
Suggest alternative JLCPCB parts for a given component.

Finds similar parts that may be cheaper, have more stock, or are Basic library type.
Useful for cost optimization and finding alternatives when parts are out of stock.

lcsc_number.description: Reference LCSC part number to find alternatives for

limit.description: Maximum number of alternatives to return

suggest_placement.name: suggest_placement
suggest_placement.description: Propose an optimized PCB footprint placement that shortens net length, orients parts toward their partners, and removes courtyard overlaps. Force-directed clustering pulls connected parts together (a converter's feedback divider and decoupling caps end up hugging its IC), power/high-current nets are weighted short & direct, and each part is rotated (0/90/180/270) to face neighbours so airwires stop crossing. PCB ONLY — does not touch the schematic. DRY RUN by default: returns proposals {ref:[x,y,rot]} plus a score (HPWL before/after, overlap counts) without modifying the board. Validate via check_courtyard_overlaps(positions=proposals), then re-run with apply=true before autoroute.

refs.description: References to move (default: every non-locked footprint on the board).

locked.description: References to hold fixed as anchors (connectors, mounting-constrained, RF, edge parts). They still pull movable parts. KiCad-locked footprints are added automatically.

apply.description: If true, move + rotate components to the proposed positions. Default false (dry run — board untouched).

grid_mm.description: Snap proposed positions to this grid (default 0.5).

spread.description: Enable density spreading (default true). Diffuses parts across free board area so a whole-board run stays legal (few/zero courtyard overlaps) instead of over-packing into a blob. Leave on for whole-board runs.

align.description: Tidy the result into rows/columns (default true). Snaps near-collinear part centers onto shared row (Y) and column (X) lines so passives line up cleanly with centers aligned — like KiCad's Align Centers + Distribute. Disable for a pure shortest-wire layout.

align_tol_mm.description: Max center spacing (mm) for parts to be pulled onto the same row/column line during align (default 1.5).

power_nets.description: Net-name fragments treated as high-current and pulled short & direct (case-insensitive). Defaults to common rails (VBAT, VBUS, VCC, 3V3, 5V, ...). Pass [] to disable.

decoupling_boost.description: Extra pull for 2-pin-passive <-> multi-pin-IC links so caps/feedback parts hug their IC (default 2.0).

bounds.description: SCOPED REGROUP: confine movable parts to this box (mm) — e.g. the area beside one IC. Combine with `refs` (that IC's passives) to regroup one cluster at a time; unlisted parts stay as anchors. Far more reliable than a whole-board run on a dense board. Default: whole board.

board_outline.description: Optional board containment bbox override. Default: derived from Edge.Cuts.

suggest_schematic_declutter.name: suggest_schematic_declutter
suggest_schematic_declutter.description: Re-orient overlapping net/global labels so their text lands in free space and becomes readable. Each label's (at x,y) anchor is its electrical connection point, so it is held FIXED — only the orientation (0/90/180/270) and justification change, throwing the text away from component bodies and other labels. Connectivity is never altered. DRY RUN by default: returns proposals [{name, at, from_angle, to_angle}] plus an overlap score (before/after) WITHOUT modifying the schematic. Set apply=true to rewrite the label orientations. (Phase 1: labels only; symbol spreading + wire reroute is a separate future capability.)

margin.description: Extra clearance in mm when testing label overlap (default 0.3).

references.description: Limit which component bodies count as obstacles (default: every component on the sheet).

apply.description: If true, rewrite the label orientations. Default false (dry run — schematic untouched, proposals only).

summarize_net_copper.name: summarize_net_copper
summarize_net_copper.description: Summarize one net's copper without listing every track, via, and zone. Returns the three counts, the layers involved, the bounding box, and a shape: vias_only, tracks_only, zones_only, empty, or mixed. vias_only means the net has vias and neither tracks nor zones. An unknown net is an error, not an empty shape.

net.description: Net name, for example GND or NetL2_1

summarize_vias.name: summarize_vias
summarize_vias.description: Count vias on the board without listing them. Returns the via count, how many run from F.Cu to B.Cu, a drill histogram, and the layer spans. Filter by net, rectangle, drill, or layer name. A stitched ground net can hold thousands of vias; this summary is the census a PDN review needs.

net.description: Only vias on this net, for example GND

boundingBox.description: Rectangle. Only vias whose centre lies inside are counted.

drillMin.description: Minimum drill diameter in millimetres, inclusive

drillMax.description: Maximum drill diameter in millimetres, inclusive

startLayer.description: Match the via start layer by the board's name or the canonical name

endLayer.description: Match the via end layer by the board's name or the canonical name

sync_schematic_to_board.name: sync_schematic_to_board
sync_schematic_to_board.description: Import the schematic netlist into the PCB board — equivalent to pressing F8 in KiCAD (Tools → Update PCB from Schematic). MUST be called after the schematic is complete and before placing or routing components on the PCB. Without this step, the board has no footprints and no net assignments — place_component and route_pad_to_pad will produce an empty, unroutable board. Works from kicad-cli's XML netlist: adds missing footprints (at the origin), swaps footprints whose schematic Footprint field changed (updateFootprints), re-nets every numbered pad (a pad its symbol has no pin for is disconnected, as in F8; generated 'unconnected-(...)' names escape '/' as {slash}), and syncs Value, Datasheet, Description and custom fields (e.g. LCSC), DNP, exclude-from-BOM and the schematic link. Footprints whose symbol is gone are always reported (footprints_without_symbol) and removed only with removeExtra=true; board-only footprints are never touched. dryRun=true returns the same report without changing or saving the board. Returns {success, dryRun, message, footprints_added, footprints_replaced, footprints_mismatched, footprints_removed, footprints_without_symbol, field_updates:[{reference, changes:[{what, from, to}]}], nets_added, pad_net_changes:[{pad, from, to}], pads_cleared, unmatched_pads, warnings}.

schematicPath.description: Absolute path to the .kicad_sch schematic file

boardPath.description: Absolute path to the .kicad_pcb board file

updateFootprints.description: Replace board footprints whose schematic Footprint field changed, keeping position, rotation, side and nets (default true). false only reports them in footprints_mismatched.

dryRun.description: Report every change without modifying or saving the board (default false)

removeExtra.description: Remove footprints whose reference is no longer in the schematic (default false: they are only reported in footprints_without_symbol). Board-only footprints are kept.

tidy_silkscreen.name: tidy_silkscreen
tidy_silkscreen.description: Re-place (and optionally resize) footprint reference designators on the silkscreen so they clear pads/mask openings, other silk, other courtyards and the board edge. Collisions use KiCad's stroke geometry (a connector's outline rectangle is four strokes, not a solid box). A reference already clear stays put (unless moveAll); others try spots around the part (body centre for large parts), at 0 or 90 degrees; one that fits nowhere is hidden (hideIfNoFit) or reported unresolved. Units mm. Returns {processed, collidingBefore, kept, moved, resized, hidden:[refs], unresolved:[refs], moves:[{ref,from,to}] (first `limit`), saved}.

textHeight.description: New text height in mm, e.g. 0.8 (JLCPCB minimum legible); omit to keep current sizes

textThickness.description: Stroke thickness in mm (default 0.15 at 0.8 mm height, scaled)

hideIfNoFit.description: Hide references that fit nowhere (default true); false leaves them and lists them as unresolved

refs.description: Only these references (default: all visible silk references)

moveAll.description: Re-place references even when already clear (default false)

includeHidden.description: Also try to place currently hidden references (default false)

gap.description: Clearance from text to pads and other silk, mm (default 0.15)

edgeClearance.description: Clearance from text to the board edge, mm (default 0.25)

largePartArea.description: Courtyard area (mm^2) from which the body centre is tried first (default 25)

courtyards.description: Keep text out of other parts' courtyards (default avoid)

limit.description: Max moves listed in the reply (default 50)

dryRun.description: Report the result without changing the board

transplant_layout.name: transplant_layout
transplant_layout.description: Copy routing (tracks, arcs, vias, zones, rule areas) from a reference .kicad_pcb around a source anchor footprint onto the loaded board around a target anchor, using the anchor-to-anchor transform (rotation + translation, mirrored when the anchors are on opposite sides; fitted to the anchor pads). First verifies every source pad in the region: a target pad must be at the transformed position (+/- tolerance) with the mapped net. A source pad lying wholly on a same-numbered target pad (an exposed pad split differently) is accepted and listed under offsetPads; a displaced pad is a padOffset mismatch. The net map is derived from the pad correspondence (anchor pins outvote passives) unless netMap is given; two-pad parts with swapped nets are reported as reversedParts. Mismatches on nets being copied abort unless force; mismatches on other nets are reported with blocking=false. `nets` restricts the copy (e.g. only the power nets). Plated holes in source pads whose target pad has none (exposed-pad via arrays) become board vias (include pad_vias). Copied vias are grown to the board's minimum via size/drill (fitVias). Items already present on the target are not duplicated. After copying it refills zones and reports pour-island splits, orphaned items (with the reason, e.g. it ended in a reference pour that was not copied), rule areas that routers treat as obstacles, net-class clearance violations and shorts to existing copper (shorts roll the copy back unless force; skipConflicting drops the offending items instead). Units mm. Returns {transform:{rotationDeg,mirrored,...}, verification:{padsChecked,padsMatched,mismatchCount,blockingCount,mismatches,offsetPads,reversedParts}, netMap:{count,derived,copied,renamed}, copied:{tracks,arcs,vias,zones,ruleAreas,padVias}, skipped:{unmappedNet,notSelected,crossingRegion,partialZones,alreadyPresent,...}, report:{pourIslands,orphaned,ruleAreas,shorts,clearance,clearanceToMatchedPads,viasResized,droppedConflicting,connectivity}, saved}.

sourceAnchorRef.description: Anchor footprint reference on the source board, e.g. U1

targetAnchorRef.description: Matching anchor reference on the loaded board, e.g. U7

netMap.description: Source net -> target net; entries not given are derived from pad correspondence

region.description: Area to copy (mm). Default: source anchor courtyard grown by regionMargin

regionFrame.description: Which board's coordinates `region` is in (default source)

regionMargin.description: Margin around the anchor courtyard for the default region, mm (default 3)

include.description: Item kinds to copy (default all). pad_vias: board vias where a source pad has a plated hole and the target pad has none

nets.description: Copy only these nets (source or target names); default every mapped net. Pad mismatches on other nets do not block

force.description: Copy despite blocking mismatches or shorts (default false)

replaceExisting.description: First remove the target's tracks/vias, zones and rule areas of the copied nets lying wholly inside the region (vias in same-net pads are kept)

fitVias.description: Grow copied vias to the board's minimum via diameter/drill/annular ring (default true)

skipConflicting.description: Drop copied tracks/vias that short or violate net-class clearance against existing copper instead of rolling back (default false)

fullNetMap.description: Include the full net map in the reply (default: only renamed nets)

limit.description: Max entries per list in the reply (default 50)

dryRun.description: Verify and report without changing the board

tune_length.name: tune_length
tune_length.description: Serpentine (meander) length tuning: replace part of straight track segments of a net with a meander that adds exactly the missing length (KiCad-style 45-degree chamfered corners by default). Target: targetLength (mm), or matchTo (a net, or a list of nets = their longest), or nets:[...] alone (tune all up to the longest). pairs:[[P,N]] tunes each pair's shorter member up to its partner with small, tight bumps. Segments are used longest first (or the given segments uuids / region); the missing length is spread over several segments if one is not enough, and the amplitude shrinks next to obstacles. Every meander is checked against other-net copper, pads, holes, keepouts, the board edge and the net's own copper (project net-class clearances) on both sides and at smaller amplitudes; segments that do not fit are skipped with a reason. Only adds length (a net longer than the target is reported, not shortened). All meanders are written in one transaction or none. Zone fills are not obstacles: refill zones and run DRC after. Units mm. Returns {allWithinTolerance, nets:[{net,targetMm,beforeMm,plannedMm,afterMm?,addedMm,remainingMm,status:'tuned'|'partial'|'notTuned'|'withinTolerance'|'tooLong',meanders,segments:[{uuid,layer,segmentLengthMm,meanders,addedMm,amplitudeMm,side}],skipped:[{uuid,reason}]}], segmentsReplaced, meanders, written}. Nothing is written with dryRun.

nets.description: Several nets to tune to the same target (default target: the longest of them)

matchTo.description: Match the length of this net, or of the longest of these nets

pairs.description: Differential pairs [positiveNet, negativeNet]: the shorter member is tuned

tolerance.description: Nets this close to the target (mm) are left alone (default 0.1)

pairTolerance.description: Allowed pair skew in mm (default: tolerance)

amplitude.description: Largest meander height from the track centre line in mm (default 1.0; pairs max(2 x width, 0.3))

spacing.description: Meander pitch (centre-to-centre of adjacent legs) in mm (default max(3 x width, width + clearance); pairs max(2 x width, width + clearance))

style.description: trombone: single-sided bumps (default); accordion: alternating sides, more length per mm; rounded: trombone with arc corners

corner.description: Corner shape: 45-degree chamfer (default), tangent arc, or square

segments.description: Only these track segments (KiCad UUIDs, e.g. from query_traces), in this order

polygon.description: Polygon vertices in mm (instead of x1..y2)

layers.description: Copper layers the region applies to (default: all)

region.description: Only place meanders whose base lies inside this rectangle/polygon (mm)

layers.description: Only tune segments on these copper layers

clearance.description: Clearance to other-net copper in mm (default: the net-class clearances; .kicad_dru custom rules are not applied, run DRC after)

allowLocked.description: Also tune locked segments (default false: they are skipped)

locked.description: Lock the new meander pieces (default false)

dryRun.description: Plan and check only; write nothing

unroute.name: unroute
unroute.description: Remove all tracks and vias of the given nets (MCP_ISSUES E1). Freerouting imports its routing locked, so pass includeLocked=true to rip that up. Returns {success, message, removed: {count, byKind, byNet}, skippedLocked?, hint?, drc?}.

limit.description: Max removed items listed (default 20)

dryRun.description: Validate and report the would-be change without touching the board

drcDelta.description: Save now and run DRC (project rules) to report violations this edit added/resolved (slower: one DRC, two when the last recorded run is stale)

refillZones.description: Refill zones in the drcDelta DRC run (default true)

projectPath.description: .kicad_pro whose rules the drcDelta DRC uses (default: the board's project)

update_graphic.name: update_graphic
update_graphic.description: Update common properties of a PCB graphic/drawing item by UUID.

update_symbol_from_library.name: update_symbol_from_library
update_symbol_from_library.description: Refresh embedded lib_symbols cache entries from a KiCad symbol library (equivalent to KiCad's Update Symbol from Library). Skips mirror-cache entries (__m0, __m90, …). Flattens (power) symbols for schematic format. Pass projectsDir to update all schematics in a folder, or schematicPath for one file.

projectsDir.description: Directory containing project subfolders with .kicad_sch files

libraryName.description: Symbol library nickname from sym-lib-table (e.g. Device, project_lib)

symbols.description: Optional: update only these symbol names (without Library: prefix)

repairMirrorFromBackup.description: Restore __m* mirror-cache lib_symbols blocks from backupDir first

backupDir.description: Backup folder with matching .kicad_sch filenames (for repairMirrorFromBackup)

validate_schematic.name: validate_schematic
validate_schematic.description: Check that a .kicad_sch file is structurally sound, reporting the line and column of every fault. kicad-cli only says whether a file loads; this says where it broke. Catches unbalanced parens, unterminated strings, trailing content, and property or effects fragments orphaned directly under (kicad_sch ...), which is what a truncated property rewrite leaves behind. A paren fault that nets to zero is caught too, by the first line whose indentation stops agreeing with its nesting depth. Note that column counts characters, so a tab counts once and the number reads lower than an editor's ruler on indented lines. Run it after any tool that edits a schematic.

runKicadCli.description: Confirm the result with kicad-cli, run on a throwaway copy so the file is never modified (default true). Set false for a fast structure-only check, or when KiCad is not installed.

validate_symbol_library.name: validate_symbol_library
validate_symbol_library.description: Check that a .kicad_sym file is structurally sound and will load, reporting the line and column of every fault instead of a bare 'Unable to load library'. Beyond paren and string structure it reports units whose names no longer match their symbol (a rename that missed the NAME_0_1 sub-symbols makes the whole library unloadable), (effects ...) or (at ...) fragments a truncated property rewrite left inside a (symbol ...), units that escaped their parent to the top level, and duplicate symbol names. Note that column counts characters, so a tab counts once and the number reads lower than an editor's ruler on indented lines. Run it after any tool that edits a library.

runKicadCli.description: Confirm the result with kicad-cli, run on a throwaway copy so the file is never modified (default true). Set false for a fast structure-only check, or when KiCad is not installed.

why_unconnected.name: why_unconnected
why_unconnected.description: Explain why a net is not fully connected: its copper islands (pads, tracks, vias and zone fills per island, biggest first) and the nearest gap between islands with coordinates. Units: mm, KiCad board coordinates (absolute positions as stored in the .kicad_pcb, +y down; not relative to a grid or aux origin). Gaps are copper-edge to copper-edge distances measured on a shared layer; when two islands share no layer the 2D gap is given with needsVia: true. The gaps form a minimum spanning tree, so closing all of them connects the net. Returns {net, fullyConnected, islandCount, islands:[{island, pads, tracks, vias, zoneFills, layers, zoneLayers?, bbox, padList}], gaps?:[{fromIsland, toIsland, gapMm, from:{at:[x,y], kind, id, layers}, to:{...}, layer? | needsVia?}], notes?}. Notes flag unfilled zones (run refill_zones) and isolated fill fragments.

net.description: Net name, e.g. GND or /Audio/LRCK (a unique last path component also works)

limit.description: Maximum islands and gaps listed (default 20)

boardPath.description: Absolute path to a .kicad_pcb to read fresh from disk. Omit to use the board loaded in memory (unsaved edits included).
